companies.name: Arthur Ventures
companies.description: Arthur Ventures is a Minneapolis, Minnesota venture capital firm that invests in early-stage B2B software companies with a global reach. The firm backs capital-efficient, founder-led software businesses across the United States and internationally, partnering with teams building enterprise and vertical SaaS, cybersecurity, developer tools, and data infrastructure. Arthur Ventures manages approximately $2B in assets under management, including roughly $800M in current active funds, and supports a portfolio of 60+ active companies. Notable portfolio investments include ThreatLocker, DNSFilter, Nucleus Security, DataCamp, Total Expert, Recast Software, CertifID, Hudu, Stream, and Macabacus. The firm is led by general partners Patrick Meenan, Ryan Kruizenga, and Andrew Heim, with offices at 250 Nicollet Mall in downtown Minneapolis.

companies.name: Atomico
companies.description: Atomico is a London-headquartered European venture capital firm founded in 2006 by Niklas Zennstrom, co-founder of Skype and Kazaa. Atomico partners with Europe's most ambitious technology founders from the earliest stages to pre-IPO across two dedicated teams: a Venture team that invests predominantly at Series A alongside occasional Seed opportunities, and a Growth team that invests from Series B to pre-IPO. In September 2024 the firm closed its largest ever fundraise, $1.24 billion across two funds - a $754M Atomico Growth VI vehicle and a $485M Atomico Venture VI vehicle - bringing total capital raised across seven funds to more than $5 billion. Growth-stage checks typically range from roughly $10M to $50M+. Atomico invests broadly across enterprise software, fintech, consumer, health, AI, developer tools, infrastructure, industrial and climate technology, with an explicit thesis that European technology has come of age. The firm operates offices in London, Paris, Berlin and Stockholm and is known for backing category-defining companies including Klarna, Stripe, Supercell, Graphcore, DeepL, Pipedrive, Truecaller, Wellhub, Lilium, Compass, Hinge Health and Sorare. Atomico also publishes the annual State of European Tech report, the definitive data-driven analysis of the European technology ecosystem.

companies.name: Bain Capital Ventures
companies.description: Bain Capital Ventures (BCV) is the venture capital arm of Bain Capital, a multi-stage, domain-focused venture business founded in 2001 with roughly $9.4B in assets under management (as of June 30, 2025). BCV incubates ideas, leads seed rounds, and scales growth-stage companies, investing from about $1M of seed capital through $100M of growth equity and partnering with more than 400 active portfolio companies. The firm concentrates on AI Apps, AI Infrastructure, Commerce, Fintech, Healthcare, Physical AI, and Security, backing companies such as MaintainX (acquired by Autodesk), Moveworks (acquired by ServiceNow), Redis, Crusoe, Cognition, Decagon, Legora, and Sunday Robotics. BCV operates from New York City, Palo Alto, and San Francisco, and pairs its investments with a "partnerships over playbooks" platform (The Hive) supporting talent, go-to-market, and customer development.

companies.name: Balderton Capital
companies.description: Balderton Capital is a London-headquartered venture capital firm focused exclusively on backing European-founded technology companies. Founded in 2000 as Benchmark Capital Europe and fully independent since 2007, Balderton is one of Europe's largest and most established venture firms, with over $7 billion in assets under management across dedicated early-stage and growth funds. The firm invests from Seed through Series B and follows on into growth stages, writing checks across sectors including fintech, artificial intelligence, B2B SaaS, developer tools and infrastructure, digital health, gaming, marketplaces and climate. Balderton is known for a founder-centric model, running a dedicated founder wellbeing and performance platform and an executive/talent network to support portfolio companies. Notable investments over the firm's history include Revolut, GoCardless, Depop, Darktrace, Contentful, Dream Games, Wayve, Aircall, Citymapper, Talend, MySQL, Recorded Future, Sophia Genetics and The Hut Group (THG).

companies.name: Battery Ventures
companies.description: Battery Ventures is a global, technology-focused investment firm founded in 1983 and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, with additional offices in San Francisco, Menlo Park, New York, London, and Tel Aviv. Battery invests across every stage of a company's life, from seed and early-stage venture through growth equity and private-equity buyouts, giving the firm a distinctive multi-stage perspective on technology markets. Its core areas of focus are application software, infrastructure software, consumer technology, and industrial tech plus life-science tools. As of 2025 the firm reports having invested in more than 530 companies over its 40-plus-year history, of which roughly 70 have gone public and another 185 have been merged or acquired. Battery is currently investing out of its 15th flagship fund, Battery Ventures XV, capitalized at $3.25 billion, and has raised more than $16 billion across all of its funds since inception. The firm describes itself as decisive, hard-working, and thesis-driven, backing category-defining companies including Affirm, Amplitude, AppDynamics, Avalara, Akamai, Coupa, Wonolo, and many others. This profile tracks Battery Ventures' identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Benchmark
companies.description: Benchmark is an American early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1995 by Bob Kagle, Bruce Dunlevie, Andy Rachleff, Kevin Harvey, and Val Vaden, and headquartered at 140 New Montgomery Street in San Francisco, California (with a second office in Woodside). Benchmark is known for its distinctive equal partnership structure, where a small number of general partners share ownership and carry equally with no junior/senior hierarchy and no managing partner. The firm concentrates on leading first institutional rounds — typically Series A — and historically kept fund sizes small (around $425M) with a focus on consumer, marketplaces, social, open source, developer tools, infrastructure, enterprise software, fintech, crypto, and artificial intelligence. Benchmark has backed transformational companies including eBay, Uber, Twitter, Instagram, Snap, Dropbox, Discord, Docker, Zendesk, Confluent, Elastic, New Relic, Asana, Amplitude, Nextdoor, Stitch Fix, Yelp, OpenTable, Zillow, Red Hat, Airtable, Benchling, Cockroach Labs, Chainalysis, HackerOne, Contentful, Modern Treasury, Stytch, and, more recently, AI-native companies such as LangChain, Cerebras, MindsDB, Lovable, Legora, Gumloop, and Starcloud. In 2026 Benchmark broke with tradition to raise roughly $2B across two new vehicles, including its first-ever dedicated later-stage growth fund. This profile tracks Benchmark's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Bessemer Venture Partners
companies.description: Bessemer Venture Partners (BVP) is one of the oldest and largest venture capital firms in the world, founded in 1911 out of the fortune of steel magnate Henry Phipps and headquartered in San Francisco, California. With more than $20 billion in assets under management and investment teams in San Francisco, Silicon Valley, New York, Boston, London, Bangalore, and Tel Aviv, Bessemer invests globally across seed, early, and growth stages, and runs a dedicated private equity buyout arm, BVP Forge. The firm invests across artificial intelligence and machine learning, cloud and infrastructure, developer tools, cybersecurity, fintech, healthcare and biotech, consumer, marketplaces, vertical software, data, deep tech and defense, and crypto/web3. Bessemer has backed transformative companies including Shopify, Twilio, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Yelp, DocuSign, Wix, Fiverr, Toast, ServiceTitan, PagerDuty, Auth0, Box, and Canva, and is known for publishing its "Anti- Portfolio" of missed opportunities, its Atlas research roadmaps, and its cloud/state-of-the-industry benchmark reports. Investing out of its 12th early-stage fund (a $3.85B vehicle), Bessemer was ranked among the largest venture firms by five-year fundraising. This profile tracks Bessemer's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Bloomberg Beta
companies.description: Bloomberg Beta is an early-stage venture capital firm that invests in companies making business work better, with a particular focus on the future of work, machine intelligence, and technologies reshaping how companies operate. Founded in 2013 and capitalized entirely by Bloomberg L.P. (though it invests independently), the firm runs approximately $450M across five $75M funds - its 2013, 2016, 2019, and 2022 vintages plus a first opportunity fund for follow-on investments in existing portfolio companies. Bloomberg Beta writes seed and early-stage checks (roughly $1M-$7M), leads or co-leads rounds, and is known for operating in public: its entire "operating manual," investment criteria, and full publicly announced portfolio live openly on GitHub, and it open-sources its Series Seed, SAFE, and note investment documents. The firm operates from San Francisco (140 New Montgomery St.) and New York (731 Lexington Ave.), backs founders across developer tools, infrastructure, security, AI, and enterprise software, and measures itself primarily on founder NPS.

companies.name: BOND
companies.description: BOND is a San Francisco-based growth-stage venture capital firm founded in 2018 by Mary Meeker, Mood Rowghani, Noah Knauf, and Juliet de Baubigny as a spinout of the Kleiner Perkins Digital Growth Fund. BOND backs proven, high-growth internet and software companies that have already established product-market fit, helping them scale globally toward IPO readiness. The firm invests primarily at the late/growth stage (roughly Series C and beyond) and is known for Mary Meeker's influential multi-hundred-page Internet Trends and AI Trends reports. Sectors span artificial intelligence, developer tools and infrastructure, fintech, health and biotech, consumer and marketplaces, and frontier hardware. BOND has raised three funds - $1.25B (2019), $2B (2021), and $2.5B (2022) - and its portfolio and track record include Canva, OpenAI, Stripe, Postman, Netlify, Revolut, Ironclad, Applied Intuition, DoorDash, Duolingo, and Uber.

companies.name: Bonfire Ventures
companies.description: Bonfire Ventures is a Los Angeles-based, seed-stage venture capital firm co-founded by Mark Mullen and Jim Andelman that invests exclusively in business-to-business (B2B) software companies, with a current focus on AI-native B2B founders. The firm runs a low-volume, high-conviction, high-support model — backing roughly 10 to 12 new companies a year, leading approximately 95% of the rounds it participates in and taking board seats — and positions itself as "AI-native too," operating an in-house AI system called Bonnie to source and support founders. Bonfire reports more than $18B in cumulative exit value across its history, with notable outcomes including TaxJar (acquired by Stripe), MNTN (IPO), The Trade Desk, Scopely, Moat (acquired by Oracle), and Comparably (acquired by ZoomInfo). It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Foundry Group and enriched from the firm's public site.

companies.name: Bullpen Capital
companies.description: Bullpen Capital is a San Francisco-based venture capital firm founded in 2010 by Paul Martino, Duncan Davidson, and Richard Melmon that pioneered the "post-seed" investment category. The firm provides early-stage financing to companies that have found initial product-market fit but are overlooked by traditional investors "for no good reason" — deliberately backing unconventional founders and sectors that other firms dismiss. Bullpen typically writes checks in the range of roughly $1M-$5M, often stepping in between the seed and Series A rounds to help capital-efficient companies push toward a strong institutional raise. The firm invests across gaming, commerce, apps and services, health, consumer and lifestyle, fintech, and marketplaces, primarily in North America with select exposure in Latin America (notably Brazil and Mexico). With a portfolio of 90+ companies, Bullpen's notable investments include FanDuel, Namely, Classy, Braze, HomeLight, ipsy, SpotHero, Splitwise, and Wag.

companies.name: Canaan Partners
companies.description: Canaan Partners is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1987 as a management buyout spin-out from General Electric's venture unit. The firm invests in "visionaries with transformative ideas," backing companies from seed through Series A across a roughly 60/40 split between technology and healthcare. On the technology side Canaan funds developer tools, security, infrastructure, fintech, consumer, AI, and frontier/deep-tech companies; on the healthcare side it specializes in de novo biotech creation, therapeutics, and medical devices. Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut with offices in San Francisco, Menlo Park, and New York City, Canaan has raised roughly $7 billion across 13 funds and is actively deploying Fund XIII. Over its 37-year history the firm reports a track record of 73 IPOs and 152 M&A exits, with notable investments including Instacart, LendingClub, The RealReal, DexCom, Match.com, Snyk, Turo, Cardlytics, and Day One Biopharmaceuticals.

companies.name: CBRE Australia
companies.description: CBRE Australia is the Australian arm of CBRE Group, the global commercial real estate services and investment firm, trading locally as CBRE (Gwsla) Pty Ltd (AU09949) and operating across the Pacific from cbre.com.au. It sits on the advisory and management side of the Australian property value chain rather than the data-infrastructure side: capital markets and investment sales, leasing and occupier advisory, valuation and advisory services, property and asset management, and project and design-and-build delivery across office, retail, industrial and logistics, build-to-rent, and alternative asset classes. Its API posture is closed. As of 26 July 2026 no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable contract, or self-serve onboarding exists for CBRE Australia: developer.cbre.com.au, developers.cbre.com.au, api.cbre.com.au, and docs.cbre.com.au do not resolve, and the global developer.cbre.com host is NXDOMAIN as well. CBRE does run API infrastructure — api.cbre.com sits behind an Imperva WAF that returns 403 to every anonymous request, api-dev.cbre.com serves a default WSO2 API Manager landing page, and eipportal.cbre.com is a login-gated "Integration Platform" SPA — but none of it is published, catalogued, or reachable by an outside developer. Commercial listings are distributed through the cbre.com.au property search and Australia's portal duopoly, and CBRE's terms of use explicitly prohibit scraping property listings from the site. RESO is absent entirely, which is the honest answer for Australia: there is no MLS here, no RESO-certified Australian organization, and the country's mandated machine-readable property rail is PEXA's electronic conveyancing network, not a RESO Web API. Access to CBRE data in Australia is a client or partner relationship, not a developer signup.

companies.name: Century 21 Canada
companies.description: CENTURY 21 Canada Limited Partnership is the Canadian master franchisor of the CENTURY 21® real estate brand, headquartered at 1285 West Pender Street in Vancouver, British Columbia. The master licence for Canada was secured in Vancouver in 1976 — the first international franchise of the CENTURY 21 System — and the network today spans roughly 400 independently owned and operated offices from coast to coast. Century 21 Canada sits in the brokerage/franchisor layer of the Canadian real estate value chain: it does not originate listing data, it consumes it. Canadian residential listings are consolidated nationally by the Canadian Real Estate Association (CREA), which runs REALTOR.ca and the Data Distribution Facility (DDF®); franchisors and brokerages redistribute that member-owned MLS® content under CREA rules rather than publishing it themselves. Century 21 Canada's API posture is accordingly empty. As of a 2026-07-26 probe there is no developer portal, no API documentation, no published base URL, no SDK, no webhooks, no Postman collection and no machine-readable contract of any kind on century21.ca or c21.ca — both century21.ca and c21.ca resolve to the same WordPress consumer site whose terms of use name MoxiWorks LLC as the site operator, and whose property search is a hosted MoxiWorks Web Marketing System surface rather than a first-party API. Wildcard DNS on *.century21.ca and *.c21.ca returns HTTP 200 for every subdomain probed (developer., developers., api., docs.) by parking them all on eboat.moxiworks.com, so those 200s are a DNS artifact and not a developer portal. RESO is absent: no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData or $metadata endpoint, and no Universal Property Identifier reference appears anywhere in the public surface — consistent with Canada, where RESO certification is not the operative seam and CREA's DDF® is. The only genuinely public, anonymously callable machine-readable surface found is the incidental WordPress REST API route index at https://www.c21.ca/wp-json/, which is a CMS artifact, is undocumented by Century 21 Canada, and is deliberately not listed here as a product API. Agent- and franchisee-facing tools live behind the hub21.ca member login. This profile is therefore identity-only and honestly records a brokerage franchisor with no published developer surface.

companies.name: Coatue Management
companies.description: Coatue Management is a global technology-focused investment manager founded in 1999 by Philippe Laffont, headquartered in New York City with offices in Menlo Park, San Francisco, London, and Hong Kong. Originally launched as a technology hedge fund, Coatue now invests across public and private markets through venture, growth, tactical (structured debt and equity), and public equities strategies, emphasizing data-driven research and responsible risk management. The firm backs disruptive, high-growth technology companies with a strong current thesis around artificial intelligence, software, cloud and data infrastructure, fintech, and frontier/space, writing checks that range from early-stage venture ($500K–$10M) through large growth and public-market allocations. Coatue managed roughly $54–55B in assets as of end of 2024 and counts Anthropic, OpenAI, Databricks, Stripe, SpaceX, Figma, and Cursor among its private portfolio companies.

companies.name: Connells Group
companies.description: Connells Limited, trading as Connells Group, is the United Kingdom's largest estate agency and property services group, headquartered at Cumbria House in Leighton Buzzard, Bedfordshire, and a wholly owned subsidiary of Skipton Building Society. It states 1,200+ branches, 16,000+ colleagues, more than 80 local brands including Connells, Countrywide, Hamptons, Sequence, Bairstow Eves, Fox & Sons, John D Wood & Co, Gascoigne Halman and Blundells, roughly 115,000 property sales a year and about 10% market share, 165,000+ managed tenancies and £33bn+ of arranged mortgage lending. It occupies almost the entire residential value chain at once: estate agency, residential and corporate lettings, new homes, land and planning, auctions, surveys and valuations, conveyancing, mortgage services, asset management, affordable housing, EPCs and inventories, commercial agency and a research and consultancy practice. Its home market is the United Kingdom, where there is no MLS and no cooperative listing standard — residential stock reaches consumers through the Rightmove and Zoopla portal duopoly by way of agency CRM and website software rather than a shared pool, and Connells' own consumer property sites are built on the Homeflow platform. Its API posture is closed and undocumented. No developer portal exists: developer., developers., api. and docs.connellsgroup.co.uk do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /.well-known/openid-configuration return 404 on both connellsgroup.co.uk and connells.co.uk. The group's 88-URL corporate sitemap contains no developer path — its one /developers/ page is addressed to property developers, not software developers. Integration is real but partner-only: Connells Survey & Valuation advertises delivering "totally integrated panel and risk management technology solutions to lenders" for the 40+ lenders whose valuation panels it manages, and reaches them through third-party platforms such as Cotality's LenderHub, while Countrywide Surveying Services' Geoconnect engine is described as connecting internal and external data sources through API integrations it consumes rather than publishes. There is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document and no Universal Property Identifier anywhere in the estate — RESO is a North American NAR/MLS mechanism and the UK has no MLS to certify against. Connells publishes no open data either; its research product, covering 88% of UK postcode areas from branch-level proprietary data, is sold through a brochure request and a contact form, and the genuinely open UK property layer belongs to the public sector (HM Land Registry Price Paid Data and Ordnance Survey), not to the brokerage.

companies.name: Costanoa Ventures
companies.description: Costanoa Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in June 2012 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with an additional office in San Francisco. Costanoa invests primarily at the Seed and Series A stages, writing checks of roughly $1M to $10M and taking concentrated 10-15% ownership across about 35 companies per fund. The firm's thesis is to fill the "missing middle" of early-stage venture by providing unusually hands-on, operator-led support to founders building applied AI, AI and data infrastructure, cybersecurity, national security / defense tech, fintech, and enterprise software companies. Costanoa was founded by Greg Sands (an early Netscape product manager) and manages roughly $2.8B in assets. In September 2024 it closed an oversubscribed Fund V at $275M alongside Opportunity Fund III at $119M, doubling down on AI-enabled B2B technology. Portfolio companies include Alation, Cyberhaven, Quizlet, PayNearMe, Auterion, Vannevar Labs, Kepler Communications, and Muon Space.

companies.name: Cowboy Ventures
companies.description: Cowboy Ventures is a seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2012 by Aileen Lee (who coined the term "unicorn" for billion-dollar startups) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The firm backs pre-seed and seed-stage founders building "life-changing" products for large and growing markets, with roughly 70% of investments made pre-product and a strong seed-to-Series A graduation rate. Typical first checks run from about $100K up to $1M, with a sweet spot near $500K–$800K. Cowboy invests across enterprise software, fintech, software infrastructure and security, healthcare, consumer, future of work, and vertical software, primarily in the United States. The firm has made 100+ early-stage investments and cultivates a curated community of founders, operators, and tech leaders. Notable portfolio companies include Chime, Guild, Drata, Dollar Shave Club, Ironclad, Aura, Kiavi, Crunchbase, and Product Hunt.

companies.name: Craft Ventures
companies.description: Craft Ventures is a San Francisco-based venture capital firm founded in late 2017 by repeat entrepreneurs David Sacks and Bill Lee, built "by founders for founders" and rooted in the operator playbook of the PayPal Mafia. The firm invests across early and growth stages, writing checks that range from micro-seed positions through double-digit millions, and specializes in B2B SaaS, marketplaces, and enterprise software prized for high-growth, high-margin, recurring-revenue economics. Craft is known for its rigorous, metrics-driven SaaS operating framework and hands-on support spanning talent, go-to-market, community, and finance. Beyond core SaaS, the portfolio spans artificial intelligence, developer tools, fintech and crypto, cybersecurity, digital health, defense, and frontier technology. The firm manages roughly $3.3 billion in assets across four early-stage funds and two growth funds, including Craft Ventures IV ($712M) and Craft Ventures Growth II ($608M). Notable investments include Airbnb, Affirm, Reddit, Uber, Lyft, Palantir, Slack, ElevenLabs, Supabase, Anduril, and Neuralink. Headquartered in San Francisco, with offices in New York City and Austin, Texas, and a primarily United States geographic focus.

companies.name: Creandum
companies.description: Creandum is a leading European early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2003 by Staffan Helgesson and headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden, with additional offices in Berlin, London, and San Francisco. The firm backs founders building global, category-defining technology companies from seed to IPO and beyond, with its tagline "we back the companies of tomorrow before it's obvious." Creandum invests across software and SaaS, artificial intelligence, fintech, consumer, marketplaces, developer tools, and infrastructure, primarily across Europe with a growing US presence. Typical investment checks range from roughly $200K to $10M, and the firm manages around $2B in assets, having closed a €500M fund to back European early-stage startups. Its portfolio of 150+ companies includes some of Europe's most successful tech businesses such as Spotify, Klarna, Depop, Trade Republic, Pleo, Neo4j, iZettle, Bolt, Kry/Livi, Lovable, and Navan. This profile tracks Creandum's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: CRV
companies.description: CRV (formerly Charles River Ventures) is one of the oldest venture capital firms in the United States, founded in 1970 to commercialize research coming out of MIT. The firm invests early — primarily at the Seed and Series A stages, with occasional Series B — leading rounds in enterprise, consumer, developer tools, security, data infrastructure, AI, and bioengineering companies. CRV has backed more than 750 companies since inception across 18 funds, raising over $4.3 billion (including a recent $600M early-stage fund), and has seen 80-plus of its portfolio companies reach public-company status. Notable investments include DoorDash, Airtable, HubSpot, Datadog, Zendesk, Patreon, Mercury, Vercel, Cursor, Postman, Kong, Tailscale, Ring, and PillPack. The firm is headquartered in San Francisco (52 Zoe Street) with a long-standing Bay Area presence and offices in Menlo Park, CA and Cambridge, MA.

companies.name: Customs Brokerage
companies.description: Customs brokerage is the licensed practice of clearing imported and exported goods through customs authorities on behalf of importers, exporters, and freight forwarders. Licensed customs brokers prepare and file entry documentation, classify merchandise under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule, calculate and remit duties and fees, manage Partner Government Agency (PGA) requirements, and represent clients in customs matters. In the United States, brokers are licensed and regulated by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP); the leading filing channel is the Automated Commercial Environment (ACE) via Electronic Data Interchange (EDI). Globally, brokerage is shaped by the WCO SAFE Framework, AEO programs, and national single-window systems. APIs in this space are typically embedded in customs broker software, freight forwarder TMS platforms, and global trade management (GTM) suites.

companies.name: D1 Capital Partners
companies.description: D1 Capital Partners is a New York City-based global investment firm founded in July 2018 by Daniel Sundheim, the former Chief Investment Officer of Viking Global Investors, who seeded the firm with more than $500 million of his own capital. The name "D1" references Amazon founder Jeff Bezos's "Day One" philosophy. D1 deploys capital across both public and private markets: in public markets it runs a global long/short equity strategy (including equity derivatives and convertible bonds) targeting medium- to long-term returns, while in private markets it takes later-stage, non-controlling growth-equity stakes in expanding companies. The firm's private portfolio spans consumer, business services, financial services, healthcare, industrials, real estate, and technology, media and telecommunications, with notable positions in companies such as SpaceX, Stripe, Anthropic, OpenAI, Ramp, Robinhood, GitLab, and Instacart. As a "Tiger Cub" descended from Viking Global, D1 grew from roughly $3 billion at launch to more than $20 billion by the end of 2020, and has been reported managing on the order of $24 billion in assets. It is headquartered at 9 West 57th Street in Manhattan.

companies.name: DCM Ventures
companies.description: DCM Ventures (formerly Doll Capital Management, and commonly known as DCM) is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1996 by Dixon Doll, a former Accel partner, and David Chao, and headquartered at 2420 Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, California with additional offices in Beijing and Tokyo. DCM was among the first Silicon Valley firms to build a cross-border, US-Asia investing practice, and typically leads early-stage rounds with checks in the roughly $1M-$5M range, deploying capital into a small group of category-defining companies each year rather than investing broadly. The firm's thesis has evolved from its original focus on communications and semiconductors toward consumer internet and SaaS, and today centers on vertical SaaS, fintech, cross-border innovation, and AI-native applications across the United States, China, Japan, and Southeast Asia. As of 2025 DCM manages approximately $4.5 billion in assets and reports 400+ portfolio companies, 35+ unicorns, and over $150 billion in aggregate market value, with notable investments including SoFi, Bill.com, Kuaishou, Matterport, 51job, Careem, and Sansan.

companies.name: DCVC (Data Collective)
companies.description: DCVC (Data Collective) is a deep-tech venture capital firm founded in 2011 and headquartered in Palo Alto and San Francisco, California. Founded and led by managing partners Matt Ocko and Zachary Bogue, DCVC backs entrepreneurs using computational and AI-driven approaches to solve trillion-dollar problems in the real world across sectors that have often seen little material progress in decades. The firm invests from early through growth stages across AI, compute and quantum, computational biology and chemistry, cybersecurity and defense, energy and climate, finance and insurance, industrial transformation and advanced manufacturing, next-gen agriculture, space, TechBio and TechMed. Across 13+ funds DCVC manages roughly $4B in assets under management (self-reported / press), making it one of the larger dedicated deep-tech franchises. Notable portfolio outcomes include companies spanning fusion energy, carbon transformation, robotics, drug discovery, and data infrastructure.

companies.name: Douglas Elliman
companies.description: Douglas Elliman Inc. (NYSE: DOUG) is a residential real estate brokerage founded in 1911 and headquartered at 575 Madison Avenue, New York City. It is one of the largest brokerages in the New York metropolitan area and among the largest in the United States, with roughly 6,000 agents across New York, Florida, California, Texas, Colorado, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Nevada, New Jersey, Vermont, the Mid-Atlantic, and international outposts in France and Monaco. Its home market is the United States. In the value chain Douglas Elliman sits on the SELL side as a licensed brokerage and MLS participant — it consumes MLS listing data under IDX and broker agreements rather than originating a syndicated feed — and it extends into development marketing, property management, commercial brokerage, title and escrow (Douglas Elliman Title), relocation, and PropTech venture investment through New Valley Ventures. Its API posture is honest and thin: no developer portal, no published API documentation, no OpenAPI or OData $metadata contract, and no published access path of any kind. developer.elliman.com, developers.elliman.com, and docs.elliman.com all resolve to the marketing homepage via a wildcard catch-all rather than to a portal, and api.elliman.com exists as an IIS/ASP.NET host that returns HTTP 403 at its root with no documentation behind it. On RESO, Douglas Elliman Real Estate is listed as a Class D member (Brokers, Agents and Appraisers) on the RESO membership roster but does NOT appear in the RESO certified-organizations directory — it is a RESO member, not a RESO-certified data provider, and it publishes no Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData endpoint, and no UPI surface. The single public engineering artifact the company ships is a GitHub fork of a third-party .NET RETS client library, which is consumer-side evidence that Elliman pulls MLS data in rather than producer-side evidence that it exposes any.

companies.name: Dragoneer Investment Group
companies.description: Dragoneer Investment Group is a San Francisco-based growth-oriented investment firm founded in 2012 by Marc Stad, a former TPG Capital and McKinsey investor. Dragoneer deploys long-duration capital across both public and private markets, concentrating on late-stage, high-growth technology companies rather than early-stage seed bets. In private markets it runs growth-equity funds that back category-leading private technology companies; in public markets it manages long-only strategy funds invested in listed technology businesses. Its capital comes from institutional limited partners including endowments, foundations, sovereign wealth funds, and family offices, and the firm is known for a patient, concentrated, founder-friendly approach that avoids traditional turnover. Dragoneer manages roughly $22B-$30B+ in assets under management (2024-2025), with sector focus spanning enterprise software, fintech and financial services, consumer internet, and artificial intelligence. The firm also sponsored a series of Dragoneer Growth Opportunities SPACs (which took CCC Intelligent Solutions and Cvent public) and is headquartered at the Letterman Digital Arts Center in San Francisco. Notable investments include Uber, Airbnb, Snowflake, Databricks, Slack, Spotify, DoorDash, Nubank, OpenAI, and Anthropic.

companies.name: Earlybird Venture Capital
companies.description: Earlybird Venture Capital is a pan-European venture capital firm founded in 1997 and headquartered in Berlin, with additional offices in Munich, London, and Milan. Earlybird identifies and backs exceptional early-stage technology companies across Europe, investing from pre-seed and seed through Series A with initial tickets up to roughly EUR 12 million, and following on through growth. The firm organizes around specialized fund streams: Digital West (Western Europe), Digital East (emerging Europe and Turkey), Health, Earlybird-X (pre-seed and university spinouts), and a pan-Earlybird Growth Opportunities fund. Its thesis spans Applications (B2B and B2C), Software Infrastructure, and DeepTech, with active investment in fintech, generative AI, deep tech, and frontier areas such as nuclear fusion and space. With more than EUR 2 billion (self-reported ~EUR 2.5B) under management, Earlybird is one of Europe's most established and active venture firms, with a track record including multiple IPOs and dozens of trade sales, and notable investments such as UiPath, N26, Aiven, Isar Aerospace, and Peak Games.

companies.name: Electric Capital
companies.description: Electric Capital is an engineering-led venture capital firm founded in 2018 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, investing in founders building frontier technologies across crypto, cryptography, distributed systems, and AI. The firm backs user-owned technology and cryptographic infrastructure that reduces reliance on intermediaries and gives users control, privacy, and access. Electric Capital invests from pre-seed through growth, with typical checks ranging from roughly $1M to $15M+, and has deployed more than $3B since inception across multiple funds (including a $1B raise announced in 2022). Its portfolio spans DeFi, layer-1 and layer-2 infrastructure, exchanges, developer tools, security, identity, and select AI, fintech, healthcare, and deep-tech companies, with notable investments including Solana, Kraken, EigenLayer/EigenCloud, dYdX, Magic Eden, Sui/Mysten Labs, NEAR, Consensys, and Aave. The firm is also known for authoring the widely cited annual Electric Capital Developer Report.

companies.name: Emergence Capital
companies.description: Emergence Capital is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2003 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, focused exclusively on early-stage B2B / enterprise software. Its founding thesis — that business software would move to the cloud — produced some of the defining SaaS bets of the era, including a contrarian 2003 investment in Salesforce and being the sole venture backer of Veeva's 2008 Series A. The firm runs a deliberately high-conviction, low-volume model in which each partner makes roughly one investment per year, enabling deep engagement with every founder. Its current thesis centers on "AI-native services" — companies that sell outcomes rather than software subscriptions, whose service margins improve as AI models improve — alongside AI infrastructure, physical-world AI, and horizontal and vertical SaaS. Emergence closed Fund VII at $1B in March 2025 (its largest fund, following Fund VI at $575M in 2021), has deployed less than $2.5B to generate $9B+ in realized returns, and its portfolio companies are collectively worth over $450B. Notable investments include Salesforce, Zoom, Veeva, Box, Bill.com, Gusto, Doximity, and Ironclad. Reported outcomes: 90%+ of early-stage investments raised successful follow-ons, 20%+ surpassed a $1B valuation, and 10%+ went public.

companies.name: EQT Ventures
companies.description: EQT Ventures is the early-stage venture capital business within EQT Group, launched in 2016 and operating out of Stockholm with investment-advisory offices in London, Berlin, Paris, Amsterdam, and the United States (San Francisco / New York); the funds themselves are domiciled in Luxembourg. The firm is a sector-agnostic, conviction-led lead investor that backs what it calls "Generation-Defining Companies" from pre-seed and seed through Series A and B, writing checks that reported ranges place between roughly EUR 1M and EUR 75M (most commonly EUR 2M-50M) and following on as companies scale. EQT Ventures has raised approximately EUR 2.3B across three funds (EQT Ventures I, II, and III) and is staffed largely by ex-founders and operators who provide hands-on support in addition to capital. Its focus spans AI, SaaS and developer tools, fintech, healthtech, climate and deeptech, robotics and aerospace, gaming, and consumer/marketplaces. Notable investments include Wolt, Depop, Typeform, AnyDesk, Netlify, Fly.io, Einride, Small Giant Games, Kry, and Beamery.

companies.name: Felicis Ventures
companies.description: Felicis Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2006 by Aydin Senkut and headquartered in Menlo Park, California. The firm backs founders "who rewrite the rules," concentrating the majority of its capital at Seed and Series A while also participating in Series B and select growth rounds, with reported assets under management of roughly $2.4B and a tenth flagship fund (FV X) of $900M closed in June 2025. Typical checks range from about $2M to $40M. Felicis is thesis-driven across artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and defense, global resilience and energy, health and bio, infrastructure, and vertical SaaS, and invests globally (backing founders from 40+ countries rather than only Silicon Valley). The firm leads or co-leads a large share of its deals, sources most new investments through founder referrals, and is known for founder-friendly practices including a commitment to vote with founders on board matters and a "1% Founder Development Pledge." Its portfolio and exits include Shopify, Adyen, Canva, Notion, Credit Karma, Fitbit, Guardant Health, Docker, PagerDuty, Twitch, Supabase, and Runway.

companies.name: Fifth Wall
companies.description: Fifth Wall is a venture capital firm founded in 2016 by Brendan F. Wallace and Brad Greiwe and headquartered in Los Angeles, California, with additional offices in New York, San Francisco, and London. It is the largest investment firm focused on technology for the built environment ("PropTech") and real estate, investing across the venture and growth stages into companies that make buildings and the physical world smarter, safer, more sustainable, and more energy efficient. The firm spans sub-themes including proptech, construction technology, residential real estate, fintech for real estate, smart buildings, logistics, and a dedicated climate/decarbonization strategy. Fifth Wall's distinctive model pairs its portfolio companies with a network of roughly 115 strategic limited partners — major real estate owner-operators such as CBRE, Hilton, Hines, Marriott, Public Storage, Related, and Starwood Capital — to drive strategic partnerships and distribution. With over $3 billion in assets under management and nearly 170 portfolio companies, Fifth Wall has backed category leaders including Opendoor, Procore, ServiceTitan, Blend, Hippo, SmartRent, and Bilt Rewards.

companies.name: First Round Capital
companies.description: First Round Capital is a seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2004 by Josh Kopelman and Howard Morgan, headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York and Philadelphia. First Round invests almost exclusively at the earliest stages of company creation, typically writing lead checks in the $750K to $4M range, and partners (many of them former founders) work side-by-side with companies through their first few years. The firm is a generalist that seeks contrarian insight into how markets work, with concentration in enterprise software, AI, fintech, healthcare, hardware, and consumer. Since founding it has backed 500+ startups and was the first institutional investor in Uber; its portfolio includes Notion, Roblox, Square, Looker, Upstart, Verkada, Warby Parker, Flatiron Health, and Clay. First Round also runs The Review, a widely read operator-focused editorial publication, and self-reports roughly $2.5B in assets under management.

companies.name: Forerunner Ventures
companies.description: Forerunner Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2012 by Kirsten Green and headquartered in San Francisco, California. Forerunner backs founders building category-defining companies, investing with early conviction at the seed and Series A stages (with selective pre-seed), typically writing initial checks in the $1M-$15M range. The firm invests across consumer, commerce, health and wellness, consumer finance, marketplaces and services, personal systems, and platforms and infrastructure, increasingly viewed through AI lenses (AI as agent, AI as infrastructure, AI as intelligence layer). Forerunner has raised nearly $3B in assets under management across seven flagship funds, with its most recent Fund VII a $500M early-stage vehicle. Its portfolio includes category leaders such as Chime, Warby Parker, Glossier, Hims & Hers, Oura, Faire, The Farmer's Dog, Dollar Shave Club, Curology, Away, Ritual, and Chime, along with a growing cohort of AI-native companies including Decagon, Suno, Slingshot AI, and Monarch Money.

companies.name: Founders Fund
companies.description: Founders Fund is a San Francisco-based venture capital firm founded in 2005 by Peter Thiel, Ken Howery, and Luke Nosek, best known for the credo "we wanted flying cars, instead we got 140 characters" and a contrarian appetite for hard science and frontier technology over incremental consumer apps. The firm backs category-defining, often monopoly-scale companies across aerospace and defense, artificial intelligence, biotech, fintech and crypto, energy, semiconductors, robotics, and deep tech, investing from seed through late-stage growth with an increasingly concentrated, high-conviction style (its recent growth funds put hundreds of millions of dollars into a small number of companies). Founders Fund manages roughly $17 billion in assets as of 2025 and is headquartered at the Letterman Digital Arts Center in San Francisco's Presidio. Its portfolio includes many of the defining technology companies of the era, among them SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Stripe, Airbnb, Facebook, Neuralink, OpenAI, DeepMind, Ramp, Nubank, Spotify, and Figma.

companies.name: Foundry Group
companies.description: Foundry Group is a Boulder, Colorado venture capital firm founded in 2007 by Brad Feld, Seth Levine, Ryan McIntyre, and Jason Mendelson. The firm invests in early-stage technology startups across the United States, organizing its work around long-lived, horizontal investment themes (such as "glue", "protocol", "distribution", and "human computer interaction") rather than narrow verticals, with a particular affinity for hardware, robotics, consumer internet, developer tools, and B2B SaaS. Foundry pioneered a "network-driven" model that operates both as a direct investor in startups and as a limited partner in a curated network of more than 40 partner venture funds. The firm manages more than $3.0B for its limited partners, has made 320+ investments and 70+ exits, and is known for radical transparency through the books, blogs, and podcasts of its partners. Notable investments include Fitbit, Zynga, SendGrid, MakerBot, Gnip, Mapbox, SeatGeek, and WHOOP. In 2022 the partners announced Foundry would not raise another fund, continuing to steward its existing funds and portfolio through their life.

companies.name: General Catalyst
companies.description: General Catalyst is a global venture capital and investment firm founded in 2000 by Joel Cutler and David Fialkow, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with offices in San Francisco, New York, London, Berlin, Bengaluru, and Washington, D.C. The firm invests across seed, venture, and growth stages and manages more than $43 billion in assets under management (as of December 2024), backing 900+ portfolio companies. General Catalyst operates through distinct capital vehicles and initiatives — Ignition/Seed for early-stage, Endurance/Grow for growth, Creation for company building, and a dedicated Health Assurance practice for healthcare transformation. Its current "Global Resilience" thesis, led by CEO Hemant Taneja, concentrates on the critical systems that underpin modern society — healthcare, energy, defense, and AI — alongside an "unscaling" thesis that uses data and AI to personalize core societal services. Notable investments include Airbnb, Stripe, Anthropic, Canva, HubSpot, Ramp, Anduril, Applied Intuition, Samsara, Mistral, Helsing, Hippocratic AI, and Mercor.

companies.name: GGV Capital
companies.description: GGV Capital (Granite Global Ventures) was a global, multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 2000 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with offices in San Francisco, Shanghai, Beijing, and Singapore. GGV invested from seed through growth stage across Social/Internet and consumer, Enterprise Tech and SaaS, and Smart Tech (fintech, infrastructure, developer tools, cybersecurity, AI, and cross-border commerce), with a distinctive US–Asia bridge thesis. At its peak the firm managed roughly $9.2B in assets under management and backed more than 400 companies, including 44 unicorns and dozens of IPOs — among them Airbnb, Slack, Square, Affirm, HashiCorp, Coinbase, Peloton, Opendoor, Poshmark, StockX, BigCommerce, Grab, Alibaba, ByteDance, Zendesk, and Xpeng. On March 29, 2024 GGV Capital ceased using the GGV brand and split into two independent successor firms amid US–China tensions: Notable Capital (US/international, led by Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon, ~$4.2B AUM) and Granite Asia (Asia, led by Jenny Lee and Jixun Foo, ~$5B AUM). The former ggvc.com companies surface now redirects to Notable Capital, which carries the US/international portfolio graph. This profile tracks GGV Capital's identity and portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: GV
companies.description: GV (formerly Google Ventures) is the venture capital arm of Alphabet, founded in 2009 by Bill Maris and headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area with additional offices in New York, Cambridge, and London. With Alphabet as its sole limited partner, GV operates with the reliability of a single LP, the autonomy of a traditional venture firm, and deep technical expertise, investing from seed through growth stage across technology and life sciences. Its focus areas span AI, enterprise, consumer, frontier tech, and life sciences, with a heavy recent emphasis on the AI frontier, from applications and developer tools to infrastructure and healthcare. GV manages over $13 billion in assets and supports roughly 400 active portfolio companies across North America, Europe, and Israel. The firm has backed notable companies including Uber, Slack, GitLab, Nest, Flatiron Health, Lemonade, Vercel, Isomorphic Labs, and insitro, with a track record of more than 80 IPOs and 230+ M&A exits.

companies.name: Hillhouse Investment
companies.description: Hillhouse Investment (formerly Hillhouse Capital) is a global investment firm founded in 2005 by Lei Zhang with seed capital from the Yale University endowment, and is one of Asia's largest private-market investors, managing an estimated US$100 billion in assets as of 2026. Headquartered in Singapore with offices in Hong Kong, Beijing, Shanghai, New York, London, and Abu Dhabi, the firm invests globally across all stages of a company's life cycle, spanning public equities, growth equity, private equity buyouts, venture capital (through its early-stage arm GL Ventures, launched in 2020), and real assets. Hillhouse describes itself as disciplined and pragmatic investors who prioritize business fundamentals and deep, bottom-up industry research, with sector focus on healthcare, industrials, energy transition, business services, and consumer. Its portfolio spans companies headquartered in more than 25 countries and has included category-defining businesses such as Tencent, JD.com, Baidu, Zoom, BeiGene, Miniso, Airbnb, Uber, and Didi. Backers have historically included major university endowments (Yale, Stanford, Princeton, MIT, University of Pennsylvania, University of Texas) and CPPIB.

companies.name: Homebrew
companies.description: Homebrew is a San Francisco-based seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2013 by Hunter Walk (a former product leader at Google and YouTube) and Satya Patel (a former VP of Product at Twitter, partner at Battery Ventures, and product leader at Google). Named after the Homebrew Computer Club, the firm practices high-conviction, concentrated seed investing, taking board-level positions and acting as an extension of the founder's team. Roughly 90% of its investments are pre-seed and seed, with initial checks in the $100K-$500K range and the ability to follow on up to $25M+ in later rounds. Homebrew backs mission-driven founders working on large, urgent, and valuable problems across fintech, AI/ML, healthcare, climate, defense, logistics, real estate, and consumer, focused on companies operating in the Americas. After a decade of institutional funds that backed companies such as Chime, Plaid, Gusto, and Mercury, Homebrew announced in 2021 that it would stop raising outside LP capital and invest only its own money going forward under the banner "Homebrew Forever."

companies.name: HongShan (HSG)
companies.description: HongShan (HSG), formerly known as Sequoia Capital China, is a leading global venture capital and private equity firm investing across technology, healthcare, and consumer sectors. Founded in 2005 by Neil Shen with early guidance from Sequoia Capital, the firm spun off as an independent entity in 2023-2024, rebranding from Sequoia China to HongShan (a pinyin romanization of its Chinese name, meaning "redwood") while retaining its original Chinese name. HSG invests across the full lifecycle - seed, venture, growth, buyout, and infrastructure - and also runs a public equities business (HCEP). The firm manages over USD 61 billion in assets (as of April 30, 2026) and has backed more than 1,700 companies since inception, with 180+ having gone public and 140+ reaching unicorn status. HSG operates from Hong Kong, Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, London, Tokyo, and Singapore. Notable portfolio companies include Alibaba, ByteDance, Meituan, Pinduoduo, BYD, Nio, Xpeng, Airwallex, Canva, Monzo, and Moderna.

companies.name: HV Capital
companies.description: HV Capital is one of Europe's leading early-stage and growth venture capital firms, headquartered in Munich with an office in Berlin. Founded in 2000 as Holtzbrinck Ventures (the venture arm associated with Verlagsgruppe Georg von Holtzbrinck), the partnership completed a management buyout and rebranded to HV Capital in 2018, establishing full operational and investment independence. The firm backs European founders with global ambitions across the full lifecycle: its Venture fund writes seed and Series A checks from roughly €500K to €10M, while its Growth fund invests through Series B and beyond with checks up to €60M and follow-on reserves reaching €100M per company. HV invests across consumer internet, enterprise software and SaaS, fintech, deep tech, healthcare, climate and energy, cybersecurity, and AI. The firm reports more than €2.8B in assets under management across nine fund generations spanning Venture and Growth, over 290 portfolio companies, and 12 IPOs. Its investment philosophy — "too new is our baseline, too bold is our reason, too complex is our edge" — reflects a willingness to back complex, category-defining companies. Early and notable investments include Zalando, Delivery Hero, FlixBus, SumUp, Depop, Scalable Capital, Enpal, and Isar Aerospace. This profile tracks HV Capital's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: ICONIQ Capital
companies.description: ICONIQ Capital is a global investment firm founded in December 2011 by Divesh Makan, Michael Anders, and Chad Boeding, headquartered in San Francisco, California with offices in Palo Alto, New York, London, and Singapore. ICONIQ operates as a hybrid family office and multi-strategy investment firm serving ultra-high-net-worth technology entrepreneurs, executives, and their families, and reports over $100B in assets under management across investment management, real assets, venture and growth, and impact strategies. Its venture arm, ICONIQ Growth, partners with founders from inception through IPO and beyond, backing category-leading technology companies across enterprise software, infrastructure, data, developer tools, fintech, security, healthcare IT, and — since 2023 — artificial intelligence as a core theme. ICONIQ Growth has invested in 140+ companies and produced notable outcomes including Snowflake, Airbnb, GitLab, HashiCorp, Datadog, Docusign, Adyen, Uber, Zoom, and Procore, alongside active AI positions in Anthropic, OpenAI, Writer, Glean, ElevenLabs, and Sierra.

companies.name: IDG Capital
companies.description: IDG Capital is a global investment firm founded in Boston in 1993 and headquartered in Hong Kong, widely recognized as one of the first foreign venture investors to enter China. Over more than 30 years it has grown into a multi-stage platform spanning venture capital, growth capital, buyout, secondary markets, and public markets, with reported assets under management of roughly $20–23 billion. The firm has backed 1,800+ companies and realized 600+ exits, employing 300+ staff (about 40% investment professionals) across 12 offices on three continents, including Hong Kong, Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Singapore, Seoul, Boston, New York, Barcelona, Muscat, and the Cayman Islands. IDG Capital concentrates on Consumer, Consumer Technology, Healthcare, and Fintech/Web3, and its portfolio includes early bets on many of China's technology leaders — Tencent, Baidu, Xiaomi, Meituan, ByteDance, and Ctrip — alongside global names such as Coinbase, Circle, Farfetch, Moncler, Acne Studios, and Insta360.

companies.name: Initialized Capital
companies.description: Initialized Capital is a seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2012 by Garry Tan, Alexis Ohanian, and Harjeet (Harj) Taggar, with offices in San Francisco and New York. The firm is hyper-focused on the seed stage, typically investing before a startup's success strikes other investors as inevitable and favoring companies that have raised little to no prior capital. Rather than thematic investing, Initialized centers its thesis on strong founding teams and acts as a de facto extended founding team from 0 to 1, providing operational support across product design, engineering, recruiting, storytelling, go-to-market, and Series A fundraising. It invests broadly across enterprise SaaS, consumer, marketplaces, fintech, crypto, healthcare, climate, hardware, real estate, and frontier/AI technology. As of 2021 the firm had raised more than $3.2B across its funds and has backed 200+ companies, including 28 unicorns such as Coinbase, Instacart, Cruise, Flexport, Reddit, Opendoor, Rippling, and Patreon, with portfolio companies creating an aggregate of over $200B in market value.

companies.name: Insight Partners
companies.description: Insight Partners is a global software-focused venture capital and private equity firm founded in 1995 by Jeff Horing and Jerry Murdock and headquartered in New York City, with additional offices in London, Tel Aviv, and Palo Alto. The firm invests in high-growth technology and software ScaleUp companies at every stage from early (Series A) through growth and late-stage pre-IPO, deploying checks that range from roughly $5M up to $500M+ and pairing capital with a dedicated in-house operations team (Insight Onsite) that provides talent, sales, marketing, and product expertise to accelerate scaling. Sector emphasis spans enterprise software broadly, including cybersecurity, fintech, AI/ML, DevOps, data infrastructure, and healthtech. With approximately $90B in regulatory assets under management as of 2025 and more than 875 companies backed worldwide, Insight is one of the largest technology investors in the world, with a portfolio and exit history that includes Twitter, Shopify, DocuSign, Wix, SentinelOne, HelloFresh, N26, Alteryx, and AppDynamics.

companies.name: Institutional Venture Partners
companies.description: Institutional Venture Partners (IVP) is a later-stage venture capital and growth equity firm founded in 1980 by Reid Dennis and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with offices in San Francisco and London. One of the oldest venture firms in Silicon Valley, IVP concentrates on the fastest-growing, most prominent late-stage and growth-stage technology companies each year, typically writing checks in the $10M to $100M range and taking a long-term view toward value creation. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, fintech, cybersecurity, developer tools and cloud infrastructure, data and AI, consumer internet, media, gaming, and healthcare. Across roughly 45 years and 18 funds (Fund XVIII closed at $1.6B in 2024) IVP has backed more than 400 companies and seen 135+ IPOs, with roughly $7B–$8B in assets under management. Notable investments and exits include Netflix, Twitter, Snap, Coinbase, Dropbox, GitHub, Slack, Datadog, CrowdStrike, HashiCorp, UiPath, Robinhood, Klarna, Wise, Figma, Grammarly, Rubrik, Discord, Anthropic, Perplexity, and DeepL.

companies.name: Keller Williams
companies.description: Keller Williams Realty, Inc. (KWRI) is an Austin, Texas headquartered residential real estate franchisor and the largest real estate brokerage franchise in the United States by agent count, operating more than 1,000 market centers worldwide through independently owned and operated offices. In the value chain Keller Williams sits at the brokerage and agent-platform layer, not the data-cooperative layer: it franchises brokerages, and it builds and operates KW Command, a proprietary agent operating system for lead, contact, task, listing, opportunity and marketing management, plus the KW Marketplace where third-party vendors sell integrated products to KW agents. Its API posture is real but partner-gated. Keller Williams runs a genuine Apigee-backed developer portal (DevHub) at developer.kw.com with a live gateway at partners.api.kw.com and a sandbox at sandbox.partners.api.kw.com, an OpenID Connect authorization server whose discovery document is publicly readable, and a published API License Agreement. Access is not self-serve: a developer must submit a partnership application through the "Apply to Integrate" form, be approved by KWRI, receive a DevHub account, then sign the KW API License Agreement and Terms of Use before receiving an API key and secret. Only one API — KW Worldwide Listings Search — is visible anonymously in the API catalog; the rest of the catalog (Command MC, Contact and Lead Data, Tasks, Opportunity/Deal/ Transaction Data, User/Organization/Role Information, Marketplace Subscription Management, Internal) is behind a SAML member login. On the sector's central question, Keller Williams carries no RESO posture at all: it is absent from the RESO certification directory, no RESO Web API, Data Dictionary, OData $metadata or Universal Property Identifier reference appears anywhere in its developer portal or specification, and its own listings spec states in its description that the service "is not a substitution for or tied to any Multiple Listings Services database records." This is a brokerage's own listing and CRM data behind a commercial partner agreement, not licensed MLS data behind a certified standard.

companies.name: Khosla Ventures
companies.description: Khosla Ventures is a Menlo Park, California venture capital firm founded in 2004 by Sun Microsystems co-founder Vinod Khosla. The firm backs bold, early, and impactful ventures, favoring contrarian deep-tech bets with world-class teams and a conviction-driven approach that deliberately accepts a high failure rate to capture transformative outcomes. Khosla invests across seed, early (Series A/B), and growth stages through its Seed Fund, Main Fund, and Opportunity (growth) Fund, writing checks that range from small seed positions to large growth rounds. Focus sectors span artificial intelligence, enterprise and consumer software, financial services and fintech, robotics and frontier/deep tech, aerospace and defense, climate and sustainability (clean energy, fusion, materials, agriculture), and digital health, medtech, diagnostics, and therapeutics. The firm manages roughly $16 billion in assets as of 2025 and is known for early investments in OpenAI, Stripe, Square/Block, DoorDash, Instacart, Affirm, Impossible Foods, GitLab, Okta, Rocket Lab, and QuantumScape. Headquarters are at 2128 Sand Hill Road, Menlo Park, CA, with a primarily United States geographic focus and select global investments.

companies.name: Kindred Ventures
companies.description: Kindred Ventures is a San Francisco-based, earliest-stage venture capital firm founded in 2014 by Steve Jang and led today as a partnership with Managing Partners Steve Jang and Kanyi Maqubela. The firm backs visionary and relentless founders building the future with technology and science, investing primarily at the pre-seed and seed stage and often partnering with entrepreneurs before a company is even formed. Kindred runs a deliberately concentrated, high-touch model of roughly 25 companies per fund, and has backed 100+ startups whose aggregate market capitalization now exceeds $200B. It invests across AI and new computing, crypto/web3, fintech, consumer, health and wellness, climate tech, mobility and logistics, and developer tools and infrastructure. With around $600M in assets under management, notable investments and exits include Uber, Coinbase, Poshmark, Reddit, Postmates, Blue Bottle Coffee, Perplexity, Tala, Magic Eden, dYdX, and PlayAI (acquired by Meta in 2025).

companies.name: Kleiner Perkins
companies.description: Kleiner Perkins is one of Silicon Valley's oldest and most storied venture capital firms, founded in 1972 by Eugene Kleiner and Tom Perkins and headquartered on Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, California, with additional offices in San Francisco and Shanghai. Across more than five decades and 21 venture funds plus 6 growth funds, the firm has invested over $10 billion and backed more than 900 ventures, including foundational companies such as Amazon, Google, Genentech, Electronic Arts, Juniper Networks, Intuit, Spotify, Figma, Robinhood, DoorDash, Duolingo and Databricks. Kleiner Perkins partners with founders from inception through IPO and beyond across early and growth stages, with seed rounds averaging roughly $4-5M and Series A rounds around $17-18M. In 2026 the firm announced its twenty-second venture fund, KP22, a $1B early-stage fund, alongside $2.5B in new growth funds. Current investment focus centers on artificial intelligence and AI safety, enterprise software, developer tools and infrastructure, healthcare and biotech, fintech, hardtech and autonomous systems, and cybersecurity, with a thesis that the right idea, team and partners can create an entirely new industry.

companies.name: Knight Frank
companies.description: Knight Frank LLP is a London-headquartered global real estate consultancy founded in 1896, structured as a partnership rather than a listed company, operating through a network of over 700 offices in more than 50 territories and best known for prime and super-prime residential agency, commercial agency and occupier services, valuation and advisory, capital markets, rural and agricultural consultancy, and the Knight Frank Research programme that publishes The Wealth Report and the Prime International Residential Index. It sits on the advisory and agency side of the property value chain rather than the data-platform side. Its home market is the United Kingdom, where there is no MLS and no cooperative listing standard — residential stock reaches consumers through the Rightmove and Zoopla duopoly by way of agency CRM software (Reapit, Alto, Street, Apex27) rather than a shared cooperative pool, so Knight Frank is a supplier into that pipe and not an operator of it. Its API posture is honest but unflattering: Knight Frank publishes no developer portal, no API programme, no developer terms, no SDK and no Postman collection, and every conventional developer entry point fails — developer., developers., docs. and apis.knightfrank.com do not resolve in DNS, and /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /api-docs all return 404 on knightfrank.com and knightfrank.co.uk. On the UK site /developers is a homonym trap: it redirects to a commercial services page for property developers and housebuilders, not software developers. What does exist, entirely unadvertised, is a real machine-readable contract. The corporate search service at api-v3.web.prd-knightfrank.com serves a live Swagger UI and an OpenAPI 3.0.1 document (11 GET/POST operations across CMSPage, IntelligenceLab, Office, Person, Search, ServiceLine and Telemetry) to anonymous clients, and those endpoints answer with real office and people-directory data without any credential. The property search and saved-property service at api-v2.web.prd-knightfrank.com is the opposite: it returns 401 and is protected by Azure AD B2C (tenant KnightFrankB2Cprod, custom policy B2C_1A_MYKFSIGNIN, scope MyKf.ReadWrite) through a first-party MSAL client for the consumer My Knight Frank account, which is an end-user login and not a developer credential. There is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document and no Universal Property Identifier anywhere in the Knight Frank estate — RESO is a North American NAR/MLS construct and the United Kingdom has no MLS to certify against. Knight Frank publishes no open data either; its research ships as PDF and web narrative, and the genuinely open UK property layer belongs to the public sector — HM Land Registry Price Paid Data and Ordnance Survey open products — not to the brokerage.

companies.name: Leadout Capital
companies.description: Leadout Capital is an early-stage venture capital fund headquartered in Portola Valley, California, founded in 2018 by Ali Rosenthal — an early Facebook business hire who drove growth of Facebook Mobile, later VP of Partnerships at Wealthfront, and previously of Goldman Sachs M&A and General Atlantic. The firm leads, co-leads, or takes a significant position in pre-seed and seed rounds, organizing its thesis around "founder-market fit": founders with a unique insight about a market, often born of the founding team's lived experience and their ability to build empathy with the customers they are innovating for. Leadout looks for products with strong network effects, unique data sets, organic and viral growth characteristics, great unit economics, and long-term defensibility. Its 46-company portfolio spans SaaS, vertical SaaS, marketplaces, healthcare, consumer and commerce, and infrastructure/developer tools, and includes Expo, Cloudsmith, Creatify AI, AtoB, R-Zero, Near Space Labs, Pavilion, Momentum, Axiom Cloud, and theCut. Leadout is a partner fund within Foundry Group's network-driven limited-partner model.

companies.name: Lightspeed Venture Partners
companies.description: Lightspeed Venture Partners is a global, multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 2000 by Barry Eggers, Christopher Schaepe, Ravi Mhatre, and Peter Nieh, and headquartered in Menlo Park, California. Lightspeed invests from seed through Series F and beyond, backing bold builders across artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, cloud and enterprise infrastructure, developer tools, fintech, consumer, gaming, and healthcare/biotech. The firm operates as a single global team across roughly a dozen offices in the United States, Europe, Israel, India, and Southeast Asia, with U.S./Europe/Israel run by Lightspeed Management Company (LSVP) and India/Southeast Asia by Lightspeed India Partners (LSIP). Lightspeed reports managing on the order of $25B+ (up to $40B+ by some self-reported figures) across the Lightspeed platform. Notable investments and exits include Anthropic, Mistral AI, ElevenLabs, Wiz, Rubrik, Cato Networks, Stripe, Affirm, Snap, Nutanix, MuleSoft, AppDynamics, Nest, Grafana, ngrok, Faire, and Navan.

companies.name: LJ Hooker
companies.description: LJ Hooker is one of the largest residential and commercial real estate brokerage and property management networks in Australia and New Zealand. Founded in Maroubra, Sydney in 1928, the franchise network reports 390 businesses and around 4,000 sales professionals, property managers and support staff, facilitated more than AUD$20 billion in property transactions during 2024, and manages roughly 100,000 properties valued at about AUD$82 billion on behalf of investors. It operates across residential sales and rentals (ljhooker.com.au), commercial (ljhcommercial.com.au), rural (ljhrural.com.au), land and projects (ljhland.com.au) and New Zealand (ljhooker.co.nz). LJ Hooker sits at the agency layer of the Australian property value chain — below the REA Group / Domain portal duopoly that distributes its listings, and upstream of PEXA electronic conveyancing and the PropTrack / CoreLogic valuation data concentration. Its API posture is honestly stated as none-published: there is no developer portal, no published API documentation, no API terms of use and no partner or data-feed programme on any LJ Hooker domain. The only programmatic surface located is an undocumented, vendor-operated website backend at api01.ljx.com.au, generated by OpenAPI Generator and consumed by the Agentpoint-built property search front end; that OpenAPI definition is not published. RESO — the Real Estate Standards Organization Web API and Data Dictionary — is a North American, NAR-driven regime with no Australian footprint, and LJ Hooker appears nowhere in the RESO certificates directory.

companies.name: Lux Capital
companies.description: Lux Capital is a New York City-based venture capital firm founded in 2000 by Josh Wolfe, Peter Hebert, and Robert Paull that backs entrepreneurs building companies at the frontier of science and technology, turning "sci-fi into sci-fact." The firm systematically mines academia and government research labs for breakthrough technologies that have matured beyond proof-of-concept but have not yet attracted mainstream venture attention, then makes long-term bets on contrarians and outsiders challenging the status quo. Lux invests primarily at early stage across three focus areas: AI and technology, defense/space/ manufacturing, and biotech/healthcare, with an emphasis on deep tech, robotics, and emerging science. The firm manages roughly $7 billion in assets under management across nine core funds, closing Lux Ventures IX at $1.5 billion in January 2026, and has invested in over 200 companies. Through Lux Labs, launched in 2024, the firm has also helped create more than 20 new companies. Notable portfolio companies include Anduril, Applied Intuition, Databricks, Cognition, Ramp, Runway, Recursion Pharmaceuticals, Planet, and Saildrone. Lux is headquartered in New York City with an additional office in Silicon Valley.

companies.name: Matrix Partners
companies.description: Matrix Partners (now branded simply "Matrix") is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1977 by Paul Ferri, investing from idea through Series A. Headquartered in San Francisco at 535 Mission Street with a long-standing East Coast office in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the firm is run by former founders and company builders who describe themselves as "contrarians who invest with conviction," backing founders with deep technical expertise and a specific vision of the future. Matrix is a generalist early-stage investor across AI / frontier tech, B2B and enterprise software, fintech, consumer, healthtech, infrastructure, and semiconductors, typically writing seed and Series A checks and leading rounds. Over nearly five decades the firm has backed foundational technology and consumer companies including Apple, HubSpot, Zendesk, Canva, Afterpay, Oculus, Fivetran, Flock Safety, Quora, Postmates, GOAT, and Suno, with a track record spanning semiconductors and networking through today's AI-native startups.

companies.name: Mayfield Fund
companies.description: Mayfield Fund is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1969 and headquartered on Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, California, with a presence in Mumbai, India. One of the oldest continuously active Silicon Valley firms, Mayfield describes itself as "people first, from inception" and reports that roughly 70% of its investments begin at company inception, positioning it as the first institutional investor for early-stage founders. The firm invests primarily at the Seed, Series A, and Series B stages across artificial intelligence, enterprise software, cloud and cybersecurity infrastructure, semiconductors, consumer and social commerce, and human and planetary health. Mayfield reports approximately $3B in assets under management (and states it has committed $3B to AI investments), has backed more than 550 companies over its history, and counts 120+ IPOs and 225+ M&A exits including Genentech, Lyft, HashiCorp, Poshmark, Marketo, Couchbase, SolarCity, Intuitive Surgical, and Compaq. In 2023 the firm raised $955M across two new funds dedicated to early-stage investing.

companies.name: McGrath
companies.description: McGrath is one of Australia's largest residential real estate brokerage networks, founded in Sydney in 1988 by John McGrath and operating a mixed company-owned and franchise network of roughly 118 offices across New South Wales, Queensland, the ACT, Victoria and Tasmania. Its business lines span residential sales, property management and rentals, projects and new-development marketing, rural and livestock, an Asia Desk for offshore buyers, and mortgage broking through Oxygen Home Loans. Listed on the ASX in 2015 as McGrath Limited (ASX:MEA), it was acquired in June 2024 by a consortium of Knight Frank Australia and New Zealand's Bayleys for A$95.5m and delisted from the ASX on 28 June 2024. McGrath sits on the demand side of the Australian property value chain: it is a brokerage that publishes listings into the REA Group (realestate.com.au) and Domain portal duopoly, settles transactions over the PEXA electronic conveyancing network, and consumes valuation data from PropTrack and CoreLogic rather than producing any of those rails itself. Its API posture is honestly nil. No developer portal exists — developer., developers., api., docs., feeds., data. and portal. subdomains of mcgrath.com.au all fail to resolve (NXDOMAIN), and /developers, /api, /docs, /api-docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /$metadata and /.well-known/openid-configuration all return HTTP 404. RESO — the only genuinely mandated machine-readable real estate contract anywhere in this study — is a North American standard driven by NAR and MLS membership; it has no Australian counterpart and McGrath has no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData surface, and no Universal Property Identifier usage. McGrath's own mcgrath.com.au robots.txt explicitly disallows /properties/ and /search/ to every crawler including GPTBot, ClaudeBot, OAI-SearchBot and PerplexityBot, which is the clearest available statement of intent: the listing inventory is a marketing asset routed to portals under commercial agreements, not a developer surface.

companies.name: Menlo Ventures
companies.description: Menlo Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1976 and headquartered in Menlo Park and San Francisco, California, that invests in transformative technology companies across the full early lifecycle. Its strategy spans "the Three Stages of Early" — Inception (validating early ideas, including via the Inception Fund and the Anthology Fund AI accelerator built with Anthropic), Venture (Series A/B), and Inflection (early growth). Menlo invests across artificial intelligence, bio and healthcare, consumer, cybersecurity, defense, fintech, infrastructure, robotics and hardware, SaaS, and supply chain and automation, primarily in North America. Over roughly five decades the firm reports backing companies that produced 85+ public companies and 170+ mergers and acquisitions, with a portfolio that includes Anthropic, Uber, Roku, Chime, Carta, Benchling, Pinecone, Netlify, and Warby Parker. In 2026 Menlo announced $3 billion in fresh capital, the largest raise in the firm's history, and reports $7.6B+ in assets under management. Its ethos is "when we invest, we're invested" — active, hands-on support beyond capital.

companies.name: Multicoin Capital
