companies.description: Multicoin Capital is a thesis-driven crypto investment firm founded in 2017 by Kyle Samani and Tushar Jain, investing in cryptocurrencies, tokens, and blockchain companies and protocols believed to be reshaping trillion-dollar markets. The firm runs a hybrid structure of a hedge fund (its multi-billion dollar Master Fund, investing in public markets, direct positions, and strategic sales) alongside several venture funds that back early-stage companies, with venture checks ranging from roughly $1M to $50M. Its Venture Fund III closed at $422 million in January 2022. Multicoin invests across open and decentralized finance (DeFi), blockchain infrastructure and Layer 1/Layer 2 protocols, decentralized physical infrastructure networks (DePIN), stablecoins and payments, real-world asset tokenization, wallets, identity, gaming, and crypto-native consumer applications, with a well-known concentration around the Solana ecosystem. The firm's phoenix logo symbolizes a new financial system rising from the ashes of the old one, reflecting its long-term, high-conviction approach to absolute returns across market cycles. Headquartered in Austin, Texas, Multicoin manages capital on behalf of family offices, foundations, endowments, and institutional investors. In February 2026 co-founder Kyle Samani stepped back from day-to-day management, with operations continuing under co-founder Tushar Jain and partner Brian Smith.

companies.name: New Enterprise Associates
companies.description: New Enterprise Associates (NEA) is one of the world's largest and longest-running venture capital firms, founded in 1977 by Dick Kramlich, Chuck Newhall, and Frank Bonsal. Headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with offices in Timonium (Maryland), New York, and London, NEA invests across the full company lifecycle — "from idea to IPO" — spanning seed, Series A, and later growth rounds. The firm has raised over $27 billion in committed capital (as of December 31, 2024) and organizes into specialized practice groups across two core sectors: technology (enterprise software, consumer, fintech, AI, infrastructure) and healthcare (biopharma, life sciences, digital health, and medical devices). NEA is known for an active, hands-on partnership model and long-term support of category-defining companies, with a portfolio that has produced many notable IPOs and acquisitions including Cloudflare, MongoDB, Robinhood, Coursera, Databricks, Plaid, and Tempus.

companies.name: Northzone
companies.description: Northzone is a multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 1996 in Oslo and now headquartered in London, with additional offices in New York, Stockholm, Berlin and Amsterdam. The firm partners with founders across the United States and Europe from Seed through Growth, positioning itself as a single long-term partner from the first check all the way to IPO, with check sizes ranging from roughly $1M to $50M. Over nearly three decades Northzone has raised 13 funds, backed more than 250 companies, produced 18 unicorns and 14 IPOs, and reports $3.1bn+ in assets under management; its most recent flagship vehicle raised approximately €1bn. Northzone invests broadly across AI, enterprise software, fintech, consumer, healthcare, climate and energy, and infrastructure and developer tools, and is known for early backing of category creators including Spotify, Klarna, Trustpilot, Kahoot!, Personio, TrueLayer, Avito and iZettle. The firm supports portfolio companies through a Platform team and a network of 500+ operators drawn from companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Stripe.

companies.name: Norwest Venture Partners
companies.description: Norwest Venture Partners is a multi-stage venture capital and growth equity investment firm founded in 1961 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with additional presence in San Francisco and subsidiaries in Mumbai, India and Tel Aviv, Israel. As of its 2024 NVP XVII fund ($3B), the firm manages more than $15.5 billion in capital and has backed over 700 companies across its history. Norwest invests across the full lifecycle — from early-stage venture through late-stage growth equity — with sector focus spanning enterprise and B2B SaaS, cloud and infrastructure, AI, fintech, healthcare and life sciences (including biotech and digital health), and consumer and lifestyle brands. The firm is known for a hands-on but non-intrusive partnership model, backing its founders with Portfolio Success programs across talent, operations, leadership, and go-to-market. Notable investments include Plaid, Uber, Spotify, Opendoor, Gong, Vuori, Kendra Scott, Casper, Udemy, Avetta, Adaptive Insights, YipitData, Babylist, Workato, and Veza.

companies.name: Obvious Ventures
companies.description: Obvious Ventures is a San Francisco-based early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2014 by Ev Williams, James Joaquin, and Vishal Vasishth, investing in entrepreneurs building "world positive" companies that solve humanity's biggest problems through technology. The firm invests across three thesis pillars: planetary health (sustainable energy, food, mobility, climate), human health and longevity (healthcare, biotech, wellness), and economic health (fintech, the future of work, robotics, and inclusive systems). Obvious writes approximately 10 new checks per year, typically $5M to $12M into seed and Series A rounds, deliberately keeping fund sizes small enough that a single durable public company can return an entire fund. It closed its fifth fund at $360,360,360 in early 2026 and has backed 90+ companies since inception, including Beyond Meat, Planet, Gusto, Recursion, Devoted Health, Diamond Foundry, and Proterra. Obvious is a Certified B Corporation headquartered at 190 Pacific Avenue, San Francisco, CA.

companies.name: Offerpad
companies.description: Offerpad Solutions Inc. (NYSE: OPAD), headquartered in Chandler, Arizona, is a United States iBuyer and licensed residential real estate brokerage that buys homes directly from sellers for cash, renovates them, and resells them, while also offering traditional listing services, a free local move, and a Renovate service. It sits in the middle of the US residential value chain as a principal-position buyer and MLS-participating brokerage in seventeen states, consuming licensed MLS listing data rather than publishing it. Offerpad's API posture is honestly minimal: there is no developer portal, no published API documentation, and no self-serve API access of any kind. The developer., developers., api. and docs. subdomains do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /api-docs all return 404. Offerpad is NOT listed in the RESO certification directory, holds no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, and serves no OData service document, $metadata document, or Universal Property Identifier. Its partner surfaces — the Direct+ investor-buyer program, the Powered By Offerpad agent partner portal, the homebuilder program and the vendor network — are human web portals gated behind an intake form and a Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement, with no programmatic interface described anywhere. The only publicly callable, self-describing API on the domain is the stock WordPress REST API of the marketing site.

companies.name: Pantera Capital
companies.description: Pantera Capital is a U.S.-based investment firm founded in 2003 by Dan Morehead (former Tiger Management head of macro trading and CFO) that pivoted in 2013 to become the first U.S. institutional asset manager focused exclusively on blockchain technology and digital assets. Headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area with offices in New York and San Juan, Puerto Rico, the firm launched the first cryptocurrency fund in the United States in 2013 and now manages roughly $3.5B-$3.8B across multiple fund strategies: a Bitcoin Fund for pure BTC exposure, an Early-Stage Token Fund, a Liquid Token Fund, a Blockchain Fund, and a series of Venture Funds for equity investments. Pantera backs token projects, exchanges, DeFi and infrastructure teams, wallets, custodians, and ecosystem builders from pre-launch token stage through growth-stage equity, writing checks from roughly $500K to $50M+ and having led about half of its 200+ investments since 2013. Notable investments include Coinbase, Circle, Ripple, Uniswap, Bitstamp, Polkadot, Near, Filecoin, StarkWare, and Ondo Finance.

companies.name: Paradigm
companies.description: Paradigm is a research-driven, frontier-technology investment firm founded in 2018 by Coinbase co-founder Fred Ehrsam and former Sequoia Capital partner Matt Huang. Headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York and Washington, DC, the firm began as one of the largest crypto-focused venture funds and has since expanded to build and invest across crypto, AI, robotics, and other technical frontiers "from first check through to public markets." Paradigm is unusual in that it is both a builder and an investor: alongside its fund it ships open-source software (Reth, Foundry, Alloy, Artemis) and incubates companies. The firm has made 130+ investments and reported roughly $12.7B in assets under management as of April 2025; it raised a $2.5B first venture fund in 2021 and announced a new $1.2B fund in July 2026 aimed at the "technical frontier" including AI and robotics. Notable portfolio companies and protocols include Uniswap, Coinbase, Stripe, Optimism, Chainalysis, Fireblocks, Blur, Monad, Kalshi, and Zipline. Managing partners include Matt Huang and Alana Palmedo.

companies.name: Partech
companies.description: 'Partech is a global, multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 1982 in Silicon Valley by European pioneers and headquartered in Paris, France, with offices in San Francisco, Berlin, Milan and Dakar. Partech invests from day one through growth via a family of dedicated funds: a Seed fund (since 2013, initial checks EUR 300k-3m), a Venture fund (Series A and Series B, EUR 5-12m, focused on B2B mission-critical software), a Growth fund (since 2015, EUR 25-70m and up to EUR 100m with LPs for European scale-ups with EUR 10-100m+ run rate), an Africa fund (since 2017, seed to Series C, EUR 1-15m across the continent) and an Impact fund (EUR 15-40m, Article 9 under SFDR). Core sectors span applicative and infrastructure SaaS, financial services and fintech/insurtech, marketplaces, consumer, healthcare, AI/ML, climate, security and cloud infrastructure. Partech backs founders across Europe, Africa and North America and has built a portfolio of hundreds of technology companies.'

companies.name: Playground Global
companies.description: Playground Global is an early-stage deep tech venture capital firm founded in 2015 by Andy Rubin, Bruce Leak, Matt Hershenson, and Peter Barrett, and headquartered at 380 Portage Ave, Palo Alto, California. The firm invests "somewhere between improbable and impossible," backing technical founders who take large technology risks and build companies from first principles. Playground concentrates on four pillars: next-gen compute (quantum computing, novel AI chip architectures, advanced interconnects, and semiconductors), automation (robotics, supply-chain and industrial automation with tangible ROI), energy transition and decarbonization, and engineered biology (AI-driven drug discovery, RNA editing, and next-generation therapies). It invests at the earliest stages, often at company formation, and operates Studio Palo Alto, a lab and prototyping environment for hardware and deep-science founders. Reported assets under management are over $1.2 billion across its funds. Notable portfolio companies include PsiQuantum, Relativity Space, Ultima Genomics, d-Matrix, Velo3D (NYSE), and MosaicML (acquired by Databricks).

companies.name: Point Nine Capital
companies.description: Point Nine Capital is a thesis-driven, early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2011 and headquartered in Berlin, Germany. It is one of Europe's best-known seed investors, specializing in B2B SaaS, B2B marketplaces, developer tools and infrastructure, fintech, digital health, and increasingly AI across digital, physical, and biological domains. Point Nine typically writes initial checks of roughly $1M-$10M (EUR 0.5M-5M) and aims to be the first institutional investor for "v0.9" founders graduating from friends-and-family capital. The firm runs a deliberately small, equal partnership in which each partner works closely with only 6-8 companies at a time to provide deep operational support. Since inception it has backed more than 160 startups across 30+ countries, including early bets on Algolia, Chainalysis, Clio, Contentful, Delivery Hero, Docplanner, Factorial, Front, Loom, Mambu, NexHealth, Revolut, Typeform, Zendesk, and Westwing, with 11+ companies reaching unicorn status.

companies.name: Polychain Capital
companies.description: Polychain Capital is a San Francisco-based investment firm founded in 2016 by Olaf Carlson-Wee, the first employee and former Head of Risk at Coinbase. The firm is dedicated exclusively to blockchain and cryptocurrency, investing in protocols, digital tokens, and early-stage crypto companies through both a liquid token hedge fund and dedicated venture capital vehicles. Polychain's thesis centers on digital assets whose scarcity derives from mathematical and cryptographic properties, and its portfolio spans layer-1 and layer-2 networks, DeFi, developer and cryptographic infrastructure, custody, exchanges, zero-knowledge and privacy technology, AI-native crypto, and stablecoins. The firm has led notable rounds including Uniswap, dYdX, Yellow Card, Arbitrum (Offchain Labs), Scroll, and EigenLayer, and its venture funds are backed by LPs including Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia Capital, Union Square Ventures, and Founders Fund. Reported assets under management have ranged from roughly $2.6B to about $5B across its funds; Polychain closed a $200M fourth venture fund in 2023 and employs a team of roughly 32 people from its San Francisco headquarters.

companies.name: Pricefinder
companies.description: Pricefinder is an Australian property intelligence and valuation platform operating

companies.name: PropTrack
companies.description: PropTrack is an Australian property data, analytics, and automated valuation business, part of REA Group. It supplies residential property data, an industry-leading AI-powered Automated Valuation Model (AVM), the PropTrack Home Price Index, and market insights drawn from more than a trillion property data points across some twelve million Australian residential properties. Its raw data is sourced from public records (State/Territory land titles offices, Valuers General, and Geoscape Australia) and proprietary sources including the realestate.com.au listing portal. PropTrack exposes this through a developer program of REST APIs — covering address suggestion and matching, property and listing data, sold-transaction search (including point-and-radius queries), automated valuations, and market metrics — documented on a hosted Stoplight developer portal and secured with OAuth 2.0. The APIs are aimed at banks, lenders, brokers, proptech platforms, and other enterprise customers integrating Australian property intelligence.

companies.name: Prosus Ventures
companies.description: Prosus Ventures is the venture-capital arm of Prosus, the Amsterdam-headquartered global consumer-internet and technology group (part of the Naspers group), founded in 2015 to make early-stage and growth-stage technology investments in high-growth markets outside the United States and China. The firm invests to "fuel the ecommerce flywheel," backing companies across food delivery, fintech, consumer services, logistics, e-commerce and marketplaces, plus a strong and growing focus on early-stage AI startups that reshape the e-commerce value chain (shopping and advertising tech, customer support, AI agents and operations) and frontier technologies such as quantum computing, robotics, space and biotech. Prosus Ventures typically invests from seed through Series B and into growth rounds, with a primary geographic focus on India, Latin America and Europe, plus activity in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and ANZ. In fiscal year 2025 the group committed and invested over $400 million across 40+ closed transactions, including roughly $88 million into AI. Its public portfolio spans 80+ companies including Meesho, Urban Company, PharmEasy, Klar, ElasticRun, BandLab, Ema, Corti and Oxford Ionics. The venture team is led by CEO Martin Tschopp with regional heads across India, Europe, Southeast Asia and the Middle East.

companies.name: QED Investors
companies.description: QED Investors is a global venture capital firm founded in 2007 by Nigel Morris and Frank Rotman, both early leaders at Capital One, and headquartered in Alexandria, Virginia. QED invests exclusively in fintech and financial-services technology, backing what it calls "pragmatic disruptors who are the future of finance" across credit and lending, banking and neobanks, banking-as-a-service and embedded finance, payments, insurance/insurtech, wealth management, proptech, and real-estate technology. The firm invests from pre-seed and seed through Series A and growth stages, with early-stage initial checks generally in the $3M-$10M range (roughly $15M average once follow-on is included) and $15M-$20M average from its growth fund. QED operates globally with investment teams across the United States, Latin America, Europe, Asia/India, and Africa, and offices in Alexandria (VA), London, Singapore, Mexico, and Brazil. It reports roughly $4B in assets under management, more than 250 portfolio companies, and over 30 unicorns, with notable investments including Nubank, Credit Karma, SoFi, Klarna, Remitly, Flywire, Klarna, Kavak, Creditas, and Bitso.

companies.name: Qiming Venture Partners
companies.description: Qiming Venture Partners is a leading China-based venture capital firm founded in 2006 by Duane Kuang and Gary Rieschel, headquartered in Shanghai with additional offices in Beijing, Suzhou, Hong Kong, Singapore, and a U.S. affiliate (Qiming Venture Partners USA) in Seattle, Washington. The firm invests at the early and growth stages, with roughly 70% of its investments concentrated in Series A and Series B rounds, across two core practice areas: Technology (mobile internet, consumer, AI, robotics, semiconductors, enterprise software, autonomous driving) and Healthcare (biotech, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, diagnostics, and digital health). Qiming manages 11 U.S. Dollar funds and 7 RMB funds with approximately $9.5 billion in capital raised, and has backed more than 580 companies, of which over 210 have exited via IPO on the NYSE, NASDAQ, HKEX, Shanghai, or Shenzhen exchanges, or through M&A. It is an early backer of some of China's most influential technology companies, including Xiaomi, Meituan, Bilibili, Zhihu, Roborock, Hesai Technology, UBTech, WeRide, Insta360, and Zhipu AI (Z.ai), alongside a deep healthcare portfolio spanning Zai Lab, Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals, CanSino Biologics, Tigermed, and Insilico Medicine.

companies.name: Ray White
companies.description: Ray White is Australasia's largest real estate group, a family-owned

companies.name: RE/MAX
companies.description: RE/MAX Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: RMAX, SIC 6531, Denver, Colorado) is one of the world's largest real estate brokerage franchisors, licensing the RE/MAX brand to independently owned and operated brokerages across more than 110 countries and territories, and franchising mortgage brokerages in the United States under the Motto Mortgage brand with loan processing through wemlo. Its home market is the United States, where it sits in the value chain as a franchisor and consumer portal operator rather than as a data owner: the listing content behind remax.com is licensed from roughly 500 local Multiple Listing Services under IDX and syndication agreements, so RE/MAX is a consumer of MLS data, not a publisher of it. Its API posture reflects that position honestly. RE/MAX is a RESO Class D member (Brokers, Agents and Appraisers) and holds a seat on the RESO Board of Directors, but it does not appear in the RESO certification directory of certified data providers and publishes no RESO Web API, no OData $metadata document and no Universal Property Identifier surface. In the United States there is no developer portal, no published API program and no machine-readable contract of any kind; developer.remax.com, developers.remax.com and docs.remax.com are only wildcard DNS entries pointing at the kvCORE agent website platform, and api.remax.com is a dangling CNAME to a decommissioned booj host that no longer resolves. The only real, publicly documented RE/MAX API surface belongs to RE/MAX Europe, whose Datahub franchise-operations API and Listings API are published as public Postman documentation with OAuth 2.0 authentication, but whose credentials are issued only to RE/MAX regional master franchisees, offices and their vendors — documented, but not self-serve. The only anonymously callable, self-describing RE/MAX endpoint family found anywhere in the estate is the WordPress REST API on the RE/MAX Europe marketing site (remax.eu/wp-json, 42 namespaces and 791 routes), which also exposes an auth-gated Model Context Protocol endpoint via the WordPress MCP Adapter — a CMS surface rather than an API product, but the closest thing to agent-accessible RE/MAX infrastructure that exists today.

companies.name: RE/MAX Canada
companies.description: RE/MAX Canada is the Canadian arm of RE/MAX, LLC, operating the remax.ca consumer portal in English and French and franchising RE/MAX brokerages across the country. Since RE/MAX Holdings closed its USD 235 million purchase of the RE/MAX INTEGRA North America regions on 2021-07-21, the Ontario-Atlantic and Western Canada regions are company-owned regions of RE/MAX, LLC, folded into RE/MAX Canada; Quebec is served separately and remax.ca robots.txt explicitly disallows /qc and /quebec. Its home market is Canada, and it sits in the value chain as a brokerage franchisor and consumer portal operator rather than as a data owner. Canadian residential listing content is cooperatively controlled by CREA and the member boards through REALTOR.ca and the Data Distribution Facility, so RE/MAX Canada displays MLS content it licenses rather than publishes; the remax.ca footer carries CREA's MLS trademark notice, and the site's home price estimates are supplied by Teranet Inc. under a personal-use-only licence that forbids commercial use, resale, external distribution and sublicensing even though Teranet's own inputs derive from public records collected by the Province of Ontario, the Province of Manitoba and the British Columbia Assessment Authority. Its API posture is recorded here honestly: there is no developer portal, no published API programme, no OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL or OData $metadata document, and no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification — a case-insensitive search of the full RESO certification directory returns zero RE/MAX matches, while 30 Canadian boards and pooled platforms do appear there. developer.remax.ca, developers.remax.ca and docs.remax.ca are wildcard DNS artifacts pointing at the kvCORE platform, proven by a control probe; api.remax.ca is a real AWS load balancer that 301-redirects every path to www.remax.ca; and the remax.ca terms of use prohibit crawlers, scripts and other automated devices outright. The only anonymously callable machine-readable RE/MAX Canada surface found is the default WordPress REST API on its WordPress VIP-hosted blog — content, not property data.

companies.name: Redpoint Ventures
companies.description: Redpoint Ventures is a Silicon Valley venture capital firm founded in 1999 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with additional offices in San Francisco and Los Angeles and a history of China-focused funds in Beijing and Shanghai. Redpoint is a multi-stage investor that backs founders from seed and early stage through growth, running dedicated early-stage and growth teams. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, AI and AI infrastructure, cloud and data infrastructure, developer tools, cybersecurity, fintech, consumer internet, healthcare, crypto/web3, and marketplaces. Typical checks range from roughly $0.5M-$2M at seed and $2M-$8M at Series A up to $10M+ at growth stage. As of 2025 Redpoint managed about $4.5 billion in assets, and its partners have participated in 130+ IPOs and acquisitions including Netflix, Snowflake, Twilio, Pure Storage, Zendesk, Stripe, HashiCorp, and HomeAway. The firm launched its tenth flagship fund, a $650M vehicle, in 2025, and publishes the annual InfraRed report on the leading private cloud and infrastructure companies. This profile tracks Redpoint's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Rentals.ca
companies.description: Rentals.ca is a Toronto-headquartered residential rental marketplace and the flagship brand of the Rentals.ca Network, which also operates Rentfaster.ca, Louer.ca, Rentboard.ca, RentCanada.com and TorontoRentals.com across more than 100 Canadian cities. The network is owned and operated by Rentsync (formerly Landlord Web Solutions Inc.), which also acquired the research firm Urbanation in January 2026 and co-publishes the monthly Rentals.ca / Urbanation National Rent Report; Rentals.ca listing data also feeds a Statistics Canada rental housing index. In the Canadian real estate value chain it sits on the rentals side of the market, outside CREA's REALTOR.ca and Data Distribution Facility, which syndicate member boards' for-sale listings. Its API posture is honest but closed: rentals.ca itself publishes no developer portal, no OpenAPI, and no documented public endpoint, and the entire consumer site sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that returns HTTP 403 to anonymous clients. The real developer surface belongs to the parent, at the Rentsync Partners portal (partners.rentsync.ca, branded "LIFT System API"), which publicly names a REST API, an Ad Syndication API and a Search API but places all documentation behind an account whose registration form requires a written application explaining what you intend to build. There is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document, no Universal Property Identifier, and no open dataset published by the company.

companies.name: Ribbit Capital
companies.description: Ribbit Capital is a venture capital firm founded in 2012 by Micky Malka and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, investing globally in founders who challenge the status quo across financial services and adjacent frontier categories. Long the most focused fintech investor in venture, Ribbit backs companies reshaping money movement, wealth management, identity, data, and global commerce, and has broadened its thesis into crypto and blockchain infrastructure, AI, and energy. The firm invests from early stage through growth, historically concentrating on Series A and B rounds while following its winners over time, and reported roughly US$12 billion in regulatory assets under management as of 2024. Ribbit's portfolio of 150+ companies spans nearly every continent and includes many of fintech's defining outcomes such as Robinhood, Coinbase, Nubank, Credit Karma, Affirm, Revolut, Brex, Mercado Libre, and Groww, alongside newer bets in crypto (Solana, Ethena, Lightspark), AI (Cognition, Etched, Decagon), and energy (Base Power, Crusoe). In 2021 Ribbit partnered with Walmart to launch the consumer fintech venture now known as OnePay.

companies.name: Royal LePage
companies.description: Royal LePage is Canada's largest residential real estate brokerage brand, founded in Toronto in 1913 as A.E. LePage and operated today under franchise and corporately-owned brokerages by Bridgemarq Real Estate Services (TSX: BRE), an affiliate of Brookfield. It spans roughly 20,000 licensed REALTORS across 600-plus offices nationwide, and sits in the value chain as a brokerage/franchisor rather than as a data platform. Its consumer search at royallepage.ca is a downstream CONSUMER of listing data, not a publisher of it - the site states its inventory is "226,755 active MLS listings via the CREA DDF network," meaning the machine-readable feed belongs to the Canadian Real Estate Association's Data Distribution Facility, not to Royal LePage. On API posture the honest finding is that there is none published for developers - no developer portal, no documented API, no OpenAPI or OData $metadata, no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification anywhere in evidence (RESO is a US NAR-adjacent regime and is simply absent from the Canadian brokerage layer), and no SDKs, webhooks, or Postman collections. Account registration on the site creates a Virtual Office Website (VOW) relationship with Royal LePage Real Estate Services, Brokerage that restricts data to personal, non-commercial use, and the legal notice expressly forbids "spiders, robots, crawlers, data mining tools, or the like." Any programmatic access to the underlying Canadian listing record runs through CREA membership and the DDF licence, not through Royal LePage.

companies.name: Sapphire Ventures
companies.description: Sapphire Ventures is a global software venture capital firm that partners with expansion-stage enterprise technology companies it believes can become category leaders. Originally founded in 1996 as the venture arm of SAP, the firm spun out as an independent company in 2011 and rebranded to Sapphire Ventures in 2014. Sapphire manages over $10 billion in assets under management and typically invests Series B through IPO, with check sizes commonly ranging from roughly $2M to $30M, while its Sapphire Sport and Sapphire Partners arms address early-stage sports/media and fund investing respectively. The firm concentrates on Enterprise AI and B2B software, including data and analytics, cybersecurity, DevOps and developer tools, fintech, health tech, and vertical SaaS. Headquartered in Austin, Texas, with offices in San Francisco, Menlo Park, New York, and London, Sapphire backs companies of consequence and supports them with a large platform team that drives executive talent and customer introductions. The portfolio spans 30+ IPOs and 80+ exits including DocuSign, Square, Wise, monday.com, JFrog, Auth0, MuleSoft, and LinkedIn.

companies.name: Savills
companies.description: Savills plc is a London-headquartered global real estate advisor, established in 1855, listed on the London Stock Exchange, with more than 42,000 people in over 70 countries. It sits on the advisory side of the property value chain rather than the data-platform side: commercial and prime residential agency, transaction advisory and capital markets, valuation and professional services, building and project consultancy, property and facilities management, rural and agricultural advisory, occupier services, the Savills Research publication programme, and a separate fund manager in Savills Investment Management. Its home market is the United Kingdom, where there is no MLS and no cooperative listing standard — residential stock reaches consumers through the Rightmove and Zoopla duopoly by way of agency CRM software (Reapit, Alto, Street, Apex27) rather than a shared cooperative pool. Savills is a supplier into that pipe, not an operator of it. Its API posture is the honest null case for this sector. Savills publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK, no Postman collection and no machine-readable contract of any kind: developer., developers., docs. and apis.savills.com do not resolve, /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /api-docs on savills.com, savills.co.uk and savills.us all return 404, and no OpenID Connect discovery document is served. Undocumented internal service hosts do exist behind the consumer property search — livev6-searchapi, livev6-authentication and livev6-profile.savills.com, named in the search application's own endpoints.js — but every one of them returns 404 to an anonymous client and none is described anywhere public. There is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document and no Universal Property Identifier anywhere in the Savills estate; RESO is a North American NAR/MLS construct and the UK has nothing to certify against. Savills publishes no open data either — its research output is PDF and web narrative, and the genuinely open UK property layer belongs to the public sector (HM Land Registry Price Paid Data and Ordnance Survey), not to the brokerage. For a developer there is no gate to pass, because there is no door: the only published route is the corporate contact form.

companies.name: Scale Venture Partners
companies.description: Scale Venture Partners (ScaleVP) is an early-stage venture capital firm based in Foster City, California, that invests primarily at Series A and Series B in founders applying AI to how businesses actually work. The firm traces its origins to 2000 as BA Venture Partners, the venture arm of Bank of America, and became an independent partnership in 2007. Scale focuses on AI and B2B software spanning applications, developer tools and infrastructure, and security, and leads roughly 80% of the rounds it joins. Initial checks typically range from $5M to $50M, sized to the round, and the firm looks for signed customers and repeatable demand (commonly $500K–$5M ARR) rather than a fixed revenue bar. Scale reports about $2.8B in assets under management and is currently deploying its $900M Fund VIII, raised in 2022. It invests across North America, Europe, and Israel, and pairs capital with a Go-To-Market advisory bench of CROs, CMOs, and CFOs. Scale has produced 11 IPOs — among the highest rates for early-stage firms — with notable investments including DocuSign, Box, HubSpot, BILL, and JFrog.

companies.name: Seedcamp
companies.description: Seedcamp is Europe's original first-cheque seed fund, founded in May 2007 and headquartered in London, United Kingdom. It backs founders from day one, writing first cheques primarily at the pre-seed and seed stages (typically between roughly $350,000 and $1 million) and following winners into later rounds through its Select fund toward Series B and beyond. Seedcamp is broadly sector-agnostic across software and technology, with concentrations in artificial intelligence, fintech, healthtech, cybersecurity, open-source, enterprise software, and developer tools. In June 2026 the firm announced it had raised $320 million — $220 million for Seedcamp VII (its flagship first cheque fund) and $100 million for the Select fund — pushing assets under management past $1 billion. The "Seedcamp Nation" now spans 500-plus companies, including publicly listed UiPath and Wise and unicorns such as Revolut, Synthesia, Sorare, Pleo, wefox, and viz.ai. Seedcamp Investment Management LLP is authorised and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority.

companies.name: Sequoia Capital
companies.description: Sequoia Capital is one of the world's leading venture capital firms, founded by Don Valentine in 1972 and headquartered at 2800 Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, California. Sequoia partners with founders from idea to IPO and beyond, investing across seed, early, and growth stages, and has backed transformative companies including Apple, Google, Oracle, Cisco, NVIDIA, PayPal, YouTube, Airbnb, Stripe, WhatsApp, Instagram, DoorDash, Snowflake, and Reddit. Its stated mission is to "help the daring build legendary companies," with a current focus on artificial intelligence and AI agents, autonomous systems, fintech, developer tools and infrastructure, healthcare, and consumer technology. Following its 2024 restructuring, Sequoia operates primarily across the US and Europe, while its former India/SEA and China arms became the independent firms Peak XV Partners and HongShan. This profile tracks Sequoia's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Shasta Ventures
companies.description: Shasta Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2004 and based in Silicon Valley (Portola Valley / Menlo Park, on and around Sand Hill Road, California). Founded by Rob Coneybeer and Ravi Mohan (with Tod Francis and Jason Pressman among its long-tenured Managing Directors), the firm invests primarily at the Series A stage in United States technology startups, typically leading rounds and taking board seats. Shasta has roughly $1.3B under management across multiple funds (Fund II $250M, Fund III $265M, Fund IV $300M) and a 20-year track record. Its thesis centers on enterprise software / SaaS, cybersecurity, developer tools and infrastructure, data intelligence, camera / computer vision, and consumer subscription products, pairing capital with operational support (Shasta Elevate) for technical founders. Notable investments include Anaplan, Zuora, Nest, Nextdoor, Apptio, Eero, Sendbird, Tonal, Lattice, Highspot, SentinelOne and Turo, with 12 unicorns, multiple IPOs and dozens of acquisitions across its history.

companies.name: Sierra Ventures
companies.description: Sierra Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded by Peter Wendell in 1982 and headquartered in San Mateo, California, in the heart of Silicon Valley. The firm invests from inception through Series A in first-principles founders under the tagline "Conviction Before Consensus," writing checks of up to $5M at seed and up to $10M at Series A. Sierra's current investment thesis centers on the next wave of enterprise technology: Vertical AI (purpose-built AI for specific industries), Infrastructure AI, Frontier and Deep Tech, and Physical AI and Robotics, alongside a longstanding history in enterprise applications, digital health, SaaS, and security. Over its 40-plus-year history the firm has invested more than $2 billion across 13 early-stage funds, with its 13th fund closing in 2023 at $265 million, following Fund 12 at $215 million and Fund 11 at $170 million. Sierra reports 35 IPOs and hundreds of successful exits, having backed companies such as Elastic, Astronomer, Chronosphere, CourseHero, Q-CTRL, Spectro Cloud, Endor Labs, and Reflection AI. The firm is notable for its CXO Advisory Board of Fortune 1000 enterprise leaders who help portfolio companies land early customers. This profile tracks Sierra Ventures' identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Slow Ventures
companies.description: Slow Ventures is a generalist early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Francisco, with additional offices in Boston and New York. The firm leads pre-seed and seed rounds, writing typical checks of roughly $500K to $3M (averaging around $1.75M), and explicitly rejects thematic investing in favor of backing experienced founders with deep, hard-won domain expertise and genuine conviction. Slow's thesis funds rapid, high-stakes experimentation: capital that tests a novel risk or hypothesis whose validation dramatically increases a company's value and that cannot easily be funded another way. As a generalist, Slow invests across consumer and social, fintech, SaaS and enterprise/developer tools, healthcare, crypto/web3, the creator economy, and real-world operations (SMB acceleration, buyouts/rollups, franchising). The firm runs a dedicated Creator Fund backing creator-led businesses, and has deployed roughly $800M+ across multiple fund vintages since inception. Notable investments include Pinterest, Slack, Robinhood, Nextdoor, Postmates, Opendoor, Wealthfront, Casper, PillPack, Airtable, Gusto, and Solana.

companies.name: Social Capital
companies.description: Social Capital is a technology investment firm founded in 2011 by Chamath Palihapitiya (a former Facebook executive) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with co-founders Mamoon Hamid and Ted Maidenberg. Originally a traditional venture fund that stood out by backing healthcare, financial services, education, and other hard, regulated sectors the VC community had neglected, the firm pivoted in 2018 into a technology holding company that stopped accepting outside capital and now invests from its own permanent balance sheet of roughly $2.1B, aiming to "earn like Berkshire Hathaway and invest like the Red Cross." Its thesis targets multiple emerging $10T markets across deep tech commercialization, life sciences and drug discovery, the global energy transition, and creator-economy media. Chamath became known as the "SPAC King" for taking companies public through the Social Capital Hedosophia (IPOA-IPOF) vehicles, including Virgin Galactic, Opendoor, Clover Health, and SoFi. Notable investments include Slack, Box, SurveyMonkey, Wealthfront, Netskope, Intercom, Groq, Palmetto, Saildrone, and Relativity Space.

companies.name: SoftBank Vision Fund
companies.description: SoftBank Vision Fund (managed by SoftBank Investment Advisers) is one of the world's largest technology-focused investment funds, launched in May 2017 by SoftBank Group and anchored by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia. Now operating across two funds (SVF1 and SVF2) with combined assets under management reported at roughly $150B+, the fund pursues Masayoshi Son's long "AI economy" thesis, backing high-growth companies across the AI stack: hardware and semiconductors, the software infrastructure to gather, process and deploy data, and the applications built on top of it. It typically writes large late-stage growth checks (Series C/D and beyond, often $100M to several billion) into 300+ companies worldwide, spanning enterprise software, consumer internet, health tech, fintech, logistics, transportation, frontier tech, edtech and proptech across the Americas, EMEA and Asia. Headquartered in London, with major offices in the US and Asia, its portfolio includes many unicorns and household names such as Arm, ByteDance, and Aurora.

companies.name: Spark Capital
companies.description: Spark Capital is a multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 2005 by Paul Conway, Santo Politi, Todd Dagres, and Bijan Sabet, with offices in San Francisco, New York, and Boston. Spark is a generalist firm that partners with founders from seed through growth across consumer internet, enterprise software, artificial intelligence, gaming, crypto, fintech, infrastructure, hardware and semiconductors, life sciences, aerospace, and the future of work. The firm invests from a family of early-stage funds (most recently a $700M fund in 2024) and dedicated growth funds (most recently a $1.4B fund in 2024), and press reports have placed its assets under management in the range of $12-15 billion. Spark first became widely known for leading Twitter's Series B in 2008 and has since backed a run of defining companies including Slack, Discord, Snap, Coinbase, Affirm, Plaid, Cruise, Oculus, Scale AI, Ramp, Deel, and Anthropic, whose Series C investment the firm turned into one of venture's largest recent markups. Spark rebranded in 2020 with design studio Pentagram around its distinctive dog-themed identity, and publishes a curated set of portfolio companies rather than a full list.

companies.name: Speedinvest
companies.description: Speedinvest is one of Europe's most active early-stage venture capital firms, founded in 2011 by Oliver Holle and headquartered in Vienna, Austria, with additional offices in Berlin, London, Munich, and Paris across EMEA. The firm invests from pre-seed and seed through selective growth stages, writing typical early-stage checks of roughly EUR 500K to EUR 3M (and up to around $10M in later rounds), and manages more than EUR 1.2 billion in assets under management. Speedinvest runs a specialist model built around dedicated sector teams rather than generalists: AI & Infra, Climate Tech & Industrial Tech, Deep Tech, Fintech & DeFi, Health & Bio, Marketplaces & Consumer, Growth, and Middle East, Africa & Beyond. Its "many move more" thesis pairs early capital with hands-on operational support, talent, customer introductions, and a global follow-on network. The firm backs technical founders across Europe and beyond, with a portfolio of 400+ companies including Bitpanda, Tide, GoStudent, Wayflyer, Curve, Adverity, Bitmovin, CoachHub, and Prewave.

companies.name: Starting Line VC
companies.description: Starting Line is a Chicago-based early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2018 by Ezra Galston that invests first checks into consumer technology startups nationwide. The firm concentrates on consumer AI, consumer health and longevity, Gen Alpha / Gen Z, consumer mobile, consumer fintech, and consumer marketplaces — as well as the infrastructure that supports them. Starting Line typically writes first checks of $500K-$1.5M (optimally $750K-$1.25M into a ~$2.5M seed round), maintains a roughly 2:1 initial-to-reserves ratio, and makes about 6-8 new investments per year. It has raised three funds — Fund I ($17M, 2018), Fund II ($30M, 2021), and Fund III ($30M, 2023) — and is headquartered in Chicago with portfolio concentrations in Los Angeles, Austin, and New York. The firm is known for radical transparency, open-sourcing its operating manual, quarterly LP letters, and mental health policy on GitHub. Notable investments include Cameo, M1 Finance, Substack, Hungryroot, Shef, Soona, SpotHero (acquired by Uber), and Pretty Litter (acquired by Mars for ~$1B).

companies.name: Stellation Capital
companies.description: Stellation Capital is a Brooklyn-based pre-seed and seed venture capital firm founded in 2021 by Peter A. Boyce II, who spent eight years at General Catalyst and co-founded its student-founder program Rough Draft Ventures. Operating under the tagline "Backing Founders At First Light" and the thesis "Present Before Proof," Stellation raised a $40M debut fund and writes first checks of roughly $250K-$2.5M, leading and co-leading rounds for "philomath" founding teams whose identities are inseparable from the problems they are solving — across AI and personal computing, fintech, consumer software, online safety, climate/energy, and consumer health. Portfolio companies include Strobe Power, Revin, Tapestry, Hopscotch (acquired by Avalara), Software Applications Incorporated, swsh, Block Party, Hearth Display, and Vybe. Stellation is also a partner fund in Foundry Group's portfolio, which is how it entered the API Evangelist network. The firm publishes no APIs; this profile carries its identity and portfolio graph.

companies.name: Susa Ventures
companies.description: Susa Ventures is a San Francisco-based early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2013 by Chad Byers, Leo Polovets, and Seth Berman on the belief that founders are the lifeblood of progress. Susa is a high-conviction, low-volume seed investor that concentrates on data-centric companies with durable competitive moats such as proprietary data, economies of scale, and network effects, and it deliberately caps each partner at a small handful of active companies so it can operate alongside founders in a late-stage, hands-on manner at the earliest stages. The firm invests primarily at pre-seed and seed (occasionally Series A), writing initial checks that typically range from roughly $1M to $5M across artificial intelligence, fintech, healthcare, logistics and supply chain, cybersecurity, developer tools and infrastructure, and consumer. Susa is known for a founder-first posture (it avoids forcing founders out) and for an unusually high seed-stage unicorn hit rate, with notable investments including Robinhood, Flexport, Andela, Newfront, Stord, Human Interest, Mux, Stedi, Viz.ai, and Casetext. The firm closed Fund V at $175M in 2025 and also runs the experimental Humba Ventures vehicle for frontier bets. This profile tracks Susa's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: SV Angel
companies.description: SV Angel is a San Francisco-based venture capital firm founded in 2009 by Ron Conway, one of Silicon Valley's most prolific angel investors. The firm runs two vehicles: an early-stage Seed Fund that writes roughly $200k checks into pre-seed and seed rounds, and a later-stage Growth Fund that invests at Series B and beyond. SV Angel is a founder-first, high-conviction investor that deliberately does not lead rounds, takes no board seats, and writes smaller checks as part of a larger syndicate so it can act as a neutral "routing layer" and advocate for founders. It is famous for its "Inflection Point Approach" — showing up at critical moments around fundraising, M&A, and business development. The firm invests almost entirely in US-based, software-driven companies across consumer and enterprise, and its portfolio has produced dozens of unicorns and landmark outcomes including Google, Airbnb, Coinbase, Stripe, Slack, Instacart, DoorDash, Reddit, Pinterest, GitHub, Databricks, Anthropic, and OpenAI.

companies.name: Techstars
companies.description: Techstars is a global pre-seed startup accelerator and investor founded in 2006 by David Cohen, Brad Feld, David Brown, and Jared Polis in Boulder, Colorado, and headquartered in New York City. Operating a worldwide network of mentorship-driven accelerator programs across cities including Boulder, Boston, Chicago, New York, London, and Tokyo, Techstars runs an intensive three-month program that provides each accepted company roughly $220,000 in capital — a $20,000 convertible equity agreement for a minimum 5% of common stock plus an optional $200,000 uncapped MFN post-money SAFE (Asia-Pacific programs at ~$100,000). The firm is largely sector-agnostic but is especially active in AI/ML, fintech, SaaS, developer tools, healthcare, climate, space and defense, and critical infrastructure, and operates on its signature "Give First" philosophy. Techstars has backed more than 10,000 founders, producing dozens of unicorns and notable companies including Twilio, SendGrid, DigitalOcean, Uber, Remitly, Chainalysis, ClassPass, DataRobot, and PillPack, with portfolio companies collectively raising tens of billions in follow-on capital.

companies.name: Threshold Ventures
companies.description: Threshold Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm based in Menlo Park, California that backs founder-led technology companies at the threshold of breakout growth. Threshold is the 2019 rebrand of Draper Fisher Jurvetson (DFJ), the storied Sand Hill Road firm founded in 1985; managing partners Emily Melton and Josh Stein spun the venture practice into an independent, focused fund. Threshold pursues a high-conviction strategy, concentrating on a small number of Series A and Series B investments and partnering hands-on with founders for the long term, frequently holding board seats through IPO and beyond. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, developer tools and infrastructure, fintech, digital health and healthcare, and AI. Its portfolio has produced 10 unicorns, 3 IPOs, and 17 acquisitions, and includes Box, Twilio, Redfin, Remitly, Doximity, Rippling, LaunchDarkly, Livongo, and Talkdesk. Threshold has invested in roughly 87 companies and raised a ~$250M fund following the rebrand.

companies.name: Thrive Capital
companies.description: Thrive Capital is a venture capital firm founded in 2009 by Joshua Kushner and headquartered in the Puck Building in New York City. The firm builds and invests in internet, software, and technology-enabled companies across the full lifecycle, from early-stage seed bets through growth and late-stage positions, and also incubates new companies through its Thrive Incubations program. Thrive concentrates its capital in a relatively small number of high-conviction positions across artificial intelligence, fintech, enterprise software, consumer internet, media and entertainment, healthcare, defense technology, and developer tools. The firm has scaled its funds steadily from a $5M first fund in 2009 to Thrive X, its tenth fund, which closed in early 2026 at over $10 billion (roughly $1B for early-stage and $9B for growth), bringing the firm to approximately $50 billion in assets under management. Nitin Nohria, the former dean of Harvard Business School, serves as executive chairman. Thrive is widely known as one of the earliest and most significant backers of OpenAI, Stripe, and SpaceX, and its portfolio includes Instagram, GitHub, Databricks, Ramp, Scale AI, Anduril, Robinhood, and Plaid.

companies.name: Tiger Global Management
companies.description: Tiger Global Management is an American investment firm founded in 2001 by Chase Coleman III, headquartered at 9 West 57th Street in New York City. It operates as a "crossover" platform that invests across both public and private markets, running a research-driven, long-term strategy to partner with high-quality, innovative technology companies across every stage of their lifecycle. Tiger Global concentrates on the global internet, software, consumer internet, and financial technology sectors, and its private/venture arm became one of the most prolific startup backers of the 2020-2022 boom, investing in 361 deals in 2021 alone and backing hundreds of growth-stage companies worldwide. Check sizes range from early-stage venture through very large growth and pre-IPO rounds, and the same team follows companies from private markets into the public markets and beyond. The firm reported roughly $55.9B in assets under management as of May 2024, and its portfolio spans North America, Europe, Latin America, India, and China. Notable investments include Stripe, ByteDance, Databricks, Coinbase, Nubank, Snowflake, UiPath, GitLab, and Flipkart.

companies.name: Trinity Ventures
companies.description: Trinity Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1986 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with more than three decades of history backing mission-driven entrepreneurs across technology and consumer markets. The firm takes a deliberately personal, low-capital-to-partner approach to early-stage investing, positioning itself as "the call you want to make, not the call you have to make" and emphasizing intellectual candor and lasting founder relationships. Trinity invests primarily at seed, Series A and Series B, with checks generally ranging from roughly $1 million to $15 million and averaging around $5 million. Its focus spans enterprise software and cloud infrastructure, developer tools, fintech, digital media and marketing technology, consumer products and services, healthcare, and artificial intelligence. Over nine funds the firm has managed on the order of $1.3 billion in assets and produced a track record that includes multiple unicorns, IPOs and roughly 130 acquisitions. Notable investments include Starbucks, New Relic, Auth0, Turo, Care.com, Zulily, Blue Nile, Aruba Networks, Infoblox, Cohesity, Outreach, InfluxData, Contentful and Docker. Trinity invests primarily in the United States.

companies.name: True Ventures
companies.description: True Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2006 by Jon Callaghan and Phil Black and headquartered in Palo Alto / San Francisco, California. Operating under a "first to believe" thesis, True writes the initial institutional check and stays invested through every subsequent stage of a company's journey, concentrating on pre-seed, seed, and Series A rounds with check sizes reported in the roughly $500K-$15M range. The firm invests broadly across technology and founder-led categories including software and developer infrastructure, consumer products and internet, healthcare and life sciences, hardware and robotics, climate and energy, security, and AI. With more than $3.8B in committed capital, True has backed 1,050+ founders across 500+ companies since inception, with notable early checks into Fitbit, Peloton, Ring, Automattic/WordPress, HashiCorp, Duo Security, Sweetgreen, Bluesky, and Splice. True is known for its founder-first platform, the True University founder camps, and long-term conviction-led early ownership.

companies.name: Uncork Capital
companies.description: Uncork Capital is a San Francisco-based seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2004 by Jeff Clavier, who formalized his angel portfolio into one of Silicon Valley's earliest dedicated seed funds; it operated as SoftTech VC until rebranding to Uncork Capital in 2017. Led by managing partners Jeff Clavier and Andy McLoughlin, the firm invests at the seed stage with a "first to believe" conviction style, typically targeting 10-15% ownership and writing seed checks broadly in the $1.5M-$4M range across B2B applications and SaaS, developer tooling, infrastructure and security, consumer and marketplaces, frontier tech/hardware, and AI/ML. In May 2025 the firm closed $300M in fresh capital across Uncork VIII (a $225M seed fund) and Uncork Plus IV (a $75M growth fund), bringing it to roughly $1.2B in assets under management. Across 275+ investments and 100+ outcomes, its portfolio and exits include SendGrid, Fitbit, Poshmark, Postmates, Eventbrite, LaunchDarkly, Tailscale, Front, Shippo, ClassDojo, Groq, Human Interest, Carrot Fertility, and GPTZero.

companies.name: Union Square Ventures
companies.description: Union Square Ventures (USV) is a thesis-driven, early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2003 by Fred Wilson and Brad Burnham and headquartered at 817 Broadway in New York City. USV invests at the edge of large markets being transformed by technological and societal pressures, historically backing large networks of engaged users that are differentiated through user experience and defensible through network effects, and more recently companies that broaden access to knowledge, capital, and well-being. The firm invests primarily at Seed and Series A across three strategies — a Core fund, a Climate fund, and an Opportunity (later-stage) fund — with check sizes typically ranging from roughly $1M at seed to the low-to-mid single-digit millions at Series A. USV runs a small, collegial partnership and focuses on social media, marketplaces, developer tools, learning/education, health, fintech, web3/decentralized protocols, energy, and climate. It reports roughly $1.9B in assets under management across 14 funds. Notable investments include Twitter, Etsy, Coinbase, Stripe, Cloudflare, MongoDB, Twilio, Duolingo, Kickstarter, Stack Overflow, SoundCloud, and Carta.

companies.name: Version One Ventures
companies.description: Version One Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in July 2012 by Boris Wertz and headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, with a partner presence in San Francisco. Run by founding partner Boris Wertz and general partner Angela Tran, the firm backs mission-driven founders who are early in new areas, writing pre-seed and seed checks where it typically leads or co-leads rounds in the roughly $500K-$1.5M range. Version One invests across marketplaces, SaaS, fintech and crypto, AI and automation, robotics and physical AI, deep tech, biology and health, and emerging-market ecosystems including India and Africa. Over more than a decade the firm has grown into a franchise of six funds and backed 100+ companies, with an early-stage track record that includes Coinbase (2021 NASDAQ direct listing), Uniswap, Dapper Labs, Ada, Jobber, Top Hat, and Shippo. In June 2026 the firm closed Version One Fund V ($78M) alongside Opportunities Fund III ($30M) for $108M in combined new capital.

companies.name: Wahi
companies.description: Wahi is a Toronto-headquartered Canadian digital real estate platform and licensed brokerage — Wahi Inc., trading as Wahi Realty Inc., Brokerage — founded in 2021 by Benjy Katchen. It runs a consumer home search, an instant home valuation estimate, market data products (Market Pulse, House Price Index), a Wahi Select REALTOR matching service and a cashback program across Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta, Nova Scotia, Saskatchewan and New Brunswick. Wahi sits in the challenger layer of the Canadian listings value chain and does not own the data it surfaces: Canadian residential listings run through CREA, the single national cooperative that operates REALTOR.ca and the Data Distribution Facility (DDF), and Wahi reaches that data as a member brokerage and through a commercial MLS connectivity vendor (Repliers) rather than by operating a feed of its own. Its real estate API posture is none-published. Probing on 2026-07-26 found no developer portal, no api./developer./developers./docs. subdomain (all fail DNS resolution), no OpenAPI or Swagger document, and no RESO Web API certification, RESO Data Dictionary certification, OData service or $metadata document anywhere on its hosts; Wahi does not appear in the RESO certificates directory nor on RESO's Canadian membership roster. The Terms of Use expressly forbid automated access, crawling and scraping, and forbid collecting, copying, storing or redistributing MLS data. The single publicly callable, self-describing API found on any Wahi host is the stock WordPress REST API of its marketing CMS — a content surface, not a real estate developer surface. Wahi is an API consumer, not an API producer.

companies.name: Wing Venture Capital
companies.description: Wing Venture Capital is an early-stage venture firm founded in 2013 by Peter Wagner and Gaurav Garg (both former partners at Sequoia Capital and Accel) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. Wing invests at the stealth, seed, and Series A stages in companies building the "AI-first" technology stack, and positions itself as a long-term company builder rather than a passive investor. Its thesis spans autonomous applications, AI and machine learning, data platforms and infrastructure, product-led growth (PLG), Web3, and bio x data. Wing raised its fourth flagship fund, Wing Four, a $600M early-stage vehicle, in 2023. Notable outcomes across its portfolio include Snowflake, Cohesity, Gong, Shape Security, and Deepgram, and it operates a Founder Success Platform plus the ET30 (Enterprise Tech 30) research program led by its research team.

companies.name: Y Combinator
companies.description: Y Combinator is the most influential startup accelerator in the world, founded in 2005 by Paul Graham, Jessica Livingston, Robert Tappan Morris, and Trevor Blackwell. Originally split between Cambridge, Massachusetts and Mountain View, California, YC consolidated in Silicon Valley and is now headquartered in San Francisco. YC runs a three-month program four times a year (winter, spring, summer, fall), each batch typically funding 250-300 early-stage startups. Its standard deal invests $500,000 in every company: $125,000 for 7% of the company on a post-money SAFE, plus $375,000 on an uncapped SAFE with a Most Favored Nation (MFN) provision. YC has funded more than 5,000 companies with a combined valuation exceeding $600 billion, including Airbnb, Stripe, Coinbase, DoorDash, Instacart, Dropbox, Reddit, Twitch, GitLab, and Ginkgo Bioworks. The firm is led by president and CEO Garry Tan, a General Partner and himself a YC alum. YC is sector-agnostic but heavily developer-tools, AI, fintech, B2B/SaaS, infrastructure, healthcare, and hard-tech oriented, and its alumni network of 6,000+ founders, plus Demo Day, Startup School, Work at a Startup, and Hacker News, form the connective tissue of the modern startup ecosystem.

companies.name: Yardi Canada
companies.description: Yardi Canada Ltd. is the Canadian subsidiary of Yardi Systems, Inc. (Goleta, California), opened in Mississauga in 1998 and now headquartered in Toronto with regional offices in Saskatoon and Vancouver and roughly 500 staff. It sells, implements and supports the Yardi property and investment management stack in Canada — Voyager, Breeze Premier, RentCafe, Home IQ, Matrix and Pulse — across residential, commercial, affordable, senior living and investment portfolios, and its Canadian footprint grew by acquisition: Point2 Technologies in Saskatoon in 2010, an EnerNOC division in Vancouver in 2016, and Planimetron in Toronto in 2022. It sits on the systems-of-record rung of the value chain rather than the listing or land-registration rung — it is the ledger and operating platform a landlord or asset manager runs on, not a portal like REALTOR.ca and not a registry operator like Teranet. Its API posture, stated honestly, is licensed-access-only and partner-gated. There is no public developer portal: developer., developers., api. and docs. hosts do not resolve on either yardi.ca or yardi.com, and the primary Canadian domain yardi.ca — registered to Yardi Systems, Inc. since 2003 — resolves to 104.156.161.80 but serves no web content at all (TCP 443 and 80 both time out). Real interfaces exist, but only behind the Interface Partnership Program: an application, a signed Data Exchange Agreement per interface type, a company at least two years old with three or more active Voyager clients, and an annual per-interface fee. RESO is absent entirely — Yardi appears nowhere in the RESO certification directory — which is the expected result for a Canadian property management vendor, because Canadian residential listings move through CREA's DDF and REALTOR.ca rather than through RESO-certified MLS endpoints.
